eQAELNKt4a.one_liner: Human-labeled benchmark for VLM judges of computer-use agent trajectories, plus open reward models (OS-Shepherd) trained on open data.
eQAELNKt4a.problem: It is unexamined whether VLM judges of computer-using agent trajectories are reliable enough to verify task completion at scale.
eQAELNKt4a.method: OSReward collects trajectories from diverse agent backbones on human-verified instructions across four platforms and labels them with ground-truth verdicts through multi-stage human annotation, with OSReward-Hard and OSReward-Multi subsets; OS-Shepherd reward models are then trained on open large-scale data.
eQAELNKt4a.key_idea: Evaluate judges on human-verdict-labeled trajectories across platforms, then train open reward models on open data to close the gap with costly judges.
eQAELNKt4a.evidence: Evaluation of VLM judges on OSReward across four platforms finds a systematic leniency bias that mislabels failed runs as successes; a few reliable judges are too costly to scale while affordable open models trail far behind.

RFvMxqnGL9.one_liner: Loops middle half of MoE Transformer layers twice, narrowing the model to match baseline FLOPs, parameters, and KV cache.
RFvMxqnGL9.problem: Looped-Transformer gains are confounded with extra per-token FLOPs, while FLOP-matched comparisons give the unlooped model more parameters, so it is unclear whether looping itself helps.
RFvMxqnGL9.method: SMELT (Sparse MoE Transformer, middle layers Loop Twice) loops the middle half of layers twice and pays for the extra layer executions by narrowing the model. Each looped model is compared with an unlooped baseline matched in per-token FLOPs, total non-embedding parameters, and KV cache.
RFvMxqnGL9.key_idea: Spend the FLOPs of repeated middle-layer execution by narrowing the model, so looped and unlooped models match in FLOPs, parameters, and KV cache.
RFvMxqnGL9.evidence: Three ablations lead to the recipe; SMELT and the baseline are scaled up to 54B total non-embedding parameters with a separate Chinchilla-style scaling law fit to each architecture.
RFvMxqnGL9.claimed_gains: SMELT saves 14.7-18.0% of training compute on the compute-optimal frontier at 10^21 FLOPs.

44QRuQVbGW.one_liner: Adapts text-to-image diffusion to infrared via frequency-aligned encoder adaptation and mean-only posterior refinement, then transfers corrections to the U-Net.
44QRuQVbGW.problem: Latent representations of pretrained text-to-image diffusion models are not tailored to infrared thermal structure and frequency characteristics, and modifying the latent space directly can break the distribution the denoiser expects.
44QRuQVbGW.method: FALA learns infrared-aware latent corrections through frequency-aligned encoder adaptation and mean-only posterior refinement, then progressively transfers them to the denoising U-Net. The authors also curate a large-scale infrared corpus from 69 datasets.
44QRuQVbGW.key_idea: Learn infrared-aware corrections in the latent encoder with frequency alignment, then progressively transfer them to the U-Net so the pretrained diffusion prior stays compatible.
44QRuQVbGW.evidence: Experiments across diverse infrared scenarios on a corpus curated from 69 datasets, reporting distribution fidelity and coverage.

JH9BScjevX.one_liner: Dual-stream video diffusion that uses optical flow as a video-native action representation for both policy and world-model modes.
JH9BScjevX.problem: World action models built on pretrained video generators need an action representation that aligns with the generator while carrying enough motion cues for control, which numerical actions and prior visual action representations do not provide.
JH9BScjevX.method: FlowWAM is a dual-stream diffusion framework in which optical flow videos share the RGB video format and are modeled jointly in a shared pretrained video generator. In policy mode it generates flow for action prediction, and in world-model mode it uses target flow sequences to guide future video generation.
JH9BScjevX.key_idea: Treat optical flow as a parallel video stream in the same pretrained generator, so actions need no separate action space and flow can be learned without action labels.
JH9BScjevX.evidence: Policy-mode evaluation on RoboTwin including pretraining on action-unlabeled videos; further results are cut off in the available abstract.
JH9BScjevX.claimed_gains: In policy mode FlowWAM outperforms both VLA and WAM baselines on RoboTwin with 93.7% average success.

mxAoSbgOth.one_liner: Unpaired unsupervised visible-infrared re-identification with attention-guided feature mapping and cross-modality positive matching
mxAoSbgOth.problem: Unpaired unsupervised visible-infrared re-identification methods overlook the identity consistency of mapped features and the effectiveness of real cross-modality positive pairs from overlapping identities.
mxAoSbgOth.method: An attention-guided feature mapping module reconstructs and weights features by cross-modality attention to preserve intra-identity consistency, a cross-modality positive matching module identifies real positive clusters from agreement between two matching results and mapped-to-target feature similarity, and multiple contrastive losses enforce identity discriminability and modality invariance.
mxAoSbgOth.key_idea: Map features across modalities with cross-modality attention weights, and accept clusters as real positives only when two cross-modality matchings agree and mapped features resemble the targets.
mxAoSbgOth.evidence: Experiments on unpaired unsupervised visible-infrared person re-identification; datasets and baselines are not stated in the visible abstract.

no9B6rTq9l.one_liner: Unified language-motion model with modality-specific Transformer towers coupled by shared attention, treating biomechanical skeleton motion as a modality
no9B6rTq9l.problem: Most multimodal human motion models use surface-driven parametric representations that do not faithfully reflect human skeletal anatomy.
no9B6rTq9l.method: OmniMM jointly models biomechanical skeleton motion, parametric motion and language using modality-specific Transformer towers coupled through shared attention over continuous motion representations. Paired parametric-biomechanics-language data are built by recovering biomechanical skeleton motion from existing SMPL sequences while preserving their annotations.
no9B6rTq9l.key_idea: Give each modality its own Transformer tower coupled through shared attention, with training data derived by recovering biomechanical skeleton motion from SMPL sequences.
no9B6rTq9l.evidence: Experiments on motion generation, understanding, bidirectional cross-representation fitting and synchronized joint generation across semantic, surface-driven and anatomy-driven motion spaces; datasets and baselines are not stated.

JETp0kGOkq.one_liner: Scores each graph by agreement with a population direction, the mean departure of other unlabeled graphs, for graph-level anomaly detection.
JETp0kGOkq.problem: Scores based on each graph's departure from learned normality can obscure structural changes that are weak in individual graphs but consistent across anomalies.
JETp0kGOkq.method: For each graph, PopGLAD estimates a reference direction from the mean departure of the remaining unlabeled graphs and measures directional agreement relative to normal variation, in structural and size views, computed from shared population summaries without pairwise graph comparisons.
JETp0kGOkq.key_idea: Score a graph by how well its departure aligns with the mean departure direction of the other unlabeled graphs, normalized by normal variation.
JETp0kGOkq.evidence: Eight graph benchmarks against GLAD baselines, with a theoretical bound on pairwise ranking error.
JETp0kGOkq.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract only claims superiority over GLAD baselines on eight benchmarks, with no numbers.

VO8iMqGA6p.one_liner: Samples proxy data mixes at capped-simplex vertices and fits a linear model whose coefficients give each domain's attribution.
VO8iMqGA6p.problem: Standard Dirichlet sampling of proxy data mixes is a poor regression design that needs tuning and cannot support a linear fit for hundreds of domains.
VO8iMqGA6p.method: LinMix samples mixes at vertices of the capped simplex, where each domain is at its cap or absent, which decorrelates domain effects and enables an interpretable linear model; the optimal mix keeps only domains with positive attribution and needs no search over candidate mixes.
VO8iMqGA6p.key_idea: Treat data mixing as domain attribution and sample proxy mixes at capped-simplex vertices, an optimal experimental design, so linear coefficients directly give domain contributions.
VO8iMqGA6p.evidence: Proofs of vertex-sampling optimality and of Dirichlet error inflation, plus pretraining experiments with 1B-parameter OLMo2 and 4B Qwen3.5 models on reasoning and other benchmarks (abstract cut off).
VO8iMqGA6p.claimed_gains: not stated numerically; the abstract says LinMix outperforms Dirichlet-based data mixing across reasoning (list cut off).

4skcCpqFmE.one_liner: Training-free self-speculative decoding for looped transformers that drafts from early recurrent depths in a pipelined, lossless scheme.
4skcCpqFmE.problem: Looped Transformers have higher decoding latency than standard models of comparable size because shared weights are accessed at every recurrent depth.
4skcCpqFmE.method: LoopSpec extracts draft tokens from early recurrent states and overlaps drafting of future tokens with verification of the current token. A selective second proposal from a deeper recurrent depth improves draft accuracy, decoding stays lossless under greedy and sampling, and optimal proposal depths are derived in closed form.
4skcCpqFmE.key_idea: Use intermediate recurrent states of a looped transformer as free draft predictions, pipelined with target verification, with proposal depths set by a closed-form optimum.
4skcCpqFmE.evidence: Reasoning and coding benchmarks across diverse Looped Transformers, with the closed-form depth predictions compared against empirical measurements.
4skcCpqFmE.claimed_gains: Up to 6.83x inference speedup across diverse Looped Transformers.

EPtfpNXW58.one_liner: HINT trains SWE agents on trajectories re-rendered under many sampled harness surfaces, reducing dependence on one tool interface.
EPtfpNXW58.problem: With model and tasks fixed, changing only the harness moves SWE-bench Verified accuracy by up to 9.0 points, and fine-tuning on one harness's trajectories teaches the interface along with the task.
EPtfpNXW58.method: They show four production harnesses reduce to the same 12 semantic actions, formalize this as the Harness Protocol that separates a protocol trajectory from a surface of tool names, documentation and formatting, and verify that rendering and parsing round-trips. HINT parses each real trajectory into the protocol and re-renders it under many sampled surfaces.
EPtfpNXW58.key_idea: Parse real trajectories into a harness-independent protocol of 12 semantic actions and re-render them under many sampled tool-name and formatting surfaces during fine-tuning.
EPtfpNXW58.evidence: Analysis of 578,856 real tool calls from four production harnesses, 1.87M render-and-parse checks with no mismatches, and SWE-bench Verified accuracy measured across harnesses.
EPtfpNXW58.claimed_gains: Harness choice alone shifts SWE-bench Verified accuracy by up to 9.0 points and single-harness fine-tuning widens the spread across harnesses from 3.4 to 11.7 points; HINT's own results are cut off in the abstract.

nsCC8uFBkj.one_liner: Benchmark of 112 professional tasks in which role-specific agent teams use tools and communicate under permission boundaries to produce deliverables.
nsCC8uFBkj.problem: Real professional work needs collaboration among coworkers with distinct responsibilities, information and permissions, but existing agent benchmarks cover this setting only to a limited extent.
nsCC8uFBkj.method: FATE, constructed by 32 domain professionals, has 112 tasks across 14 domains and 129 occupations, both unimodal and multimodal. Agents use tools and communicate under role-specific resource and permission boundaries to produce intermediate artifacts and final deliverables.
nsCC8uFBkj.key_idea: Assign agents distinct professional roles with separate information and permissions, so teams must communicate through protocols to jointly produce artifacts.
nsCC8uFBkj.evidence: Eight LLMs evaluated and four communication protocols compared on 112 tasks.
nsCC8uFBkj.claimed_gains: Current agent teams achieve a best final evaluation score of only 42.0, with limited collaboration gains at substantial computational cost.

IJiSFv0Tly.one_liner: Region-specific LoRA experts on a shared lightweight language model, with a classifier routing addresses to geocoding experts, for global geocoding.
IJiSFv0Tly.problem: Geocoding APIs are costly with substantial deployment overhead, and current models struggle to combine global coverage with robustness to complex inputs.
IJiSFv0Tly.method: GeoExperts divides the world into regions by address system and trains specialized experts on a shared lightweight language model. An address classification expert routes each request to the right geocoding expert, which maps structured addresses to latitude and longitude, while a semantic understanding expert converts natural-language text into normalized addresses.
IJiSFv0Tly.key_idea: Specialize LoRA experts per regional address system and route each request through an address classifier, with a semantic expert normalizing natural-language inputs into addresses.
IJiSFv0Tly.evidence: The new GeoMosaic dataset and the GeoMosaic-Bench benchmark of 40K samples, covering direct geocoding, input robustness and semantic location reasoning; the abstract is cut off before results.

HgFXgrR56Y.one_liner: Single-pair one-step generator training with distance-scaled attraction and repulsion displacements and shared-time noise interpolation around each positive.
HgFXgrR56Y.problem: Drifting Models need many real and generated samples per condition and large batches to estimate attraction and repulsion fields, and with one positive and one negative the normalized field ignores where the current output lies relative to them.
HgFXgrR56Y.method: Flow-Coupled Drifting scales attraction and repulsion displacements separately by their distances from the current output, giving a force whose expectation is proportional to the 2-Wasserstein gradient-flow velocity of a smoothed energy distance in pretrained feature spaces. It pairs each input with its own positive by interpolating that positive with two independent Gaussian noises at a shared time, and also trains at the pure-noise endpoint.
HgFXgrR56Y.key_idea: Scale attraction and repulsion displacements by distance to the current output, and form the output and negative from the same positive interpolated with independent noises at a shared time.
HgFXgrR56Y.evidence: Class-conditional ImageNet 256x256, adapting pretrained SiT models into one-step generators.
HgFXgrR56Y.claimed_gains: Adapts pretrained SiT models into one-step generators that achieve an FID of 1.38 on class-conditional ImageNet 256x256.

2kmexwyXHg.one_liner: Degree-aware GPU kernels for gSpMM and gSDDMM that bucket and reorder nodes, slice heavy neighborhoods, and load data asynchronously.
2kmexwyXHg.problem: On heavy-tailed real graphs, GNN kernels that give every node one unit of parallel work wait on the few highest-degree nodes while the rest of the GPU idles, and IO-aware kernels cover only a few fixed layers.
2kmexwyXHg.method: Nodes are bucketed by degree, reordered within buckets and processed concurrently so long jobs start first, the heaviest neighborhoods are cut into fixed-size edge slices merged exactly, and loads are made asynchronous to overlap computation. The techniques are provided for gSpMM and gSDDMM as a portable library of 18 and 32 kernels with autograd, from which GNN convolutions are composed in PyTorch.
2kmexwyXHg.key_idea: Balance GPU work by degree-aware partitioning: schedule long node jobs first, split heavy neighborhoods into exactly merged edge slices, and partition per-edge computations over edges.
2kmexwyXHg.evidence: Comparison against DGL on real graphs, with a library of 18 gSpMM and 32 gSDDMM kernels; the abstract is cut off before the results.

B0oyr1Zdjv.one_liner: On-policy draft-model training that directly maximizes expected accepted length, with prefix-aware credit assignment, for speculative decoding.
B0oyr1Zdjv.problem: Draft training optimizes token-level distribution alignment, which does not directly optimize accepted prefix length because one rejection discards all subsequent draft tokens.
B0oyr1Zdjv.method: FReDraft maximizes the expected accepted length of drafts sampled from the current draft model, weighting each token by its contribution to current and later acceptances. It analytically marginalizes token-level acceptance rate with the target model's vocabulary distribution to cut gradient variance, and shifts part of that gradient into an explicit penalty on sampled tokens whose probabilities the draft overestimates.
B0oyr1Zdjv.key_idea: Optimize expected accepted length under first-rejection truncation, using analytically marginalized acceptance rates for low-variance, prefix-aware gradients.
B0oyr1Zdjv.evidence: Experiments across multiple benchmarks and target models against strong baselines; specific datasets and models are not named.
B0oyr1Zdjv.claimed_gains: Improves accepted length and decoding speedup over strong baselines and converges faster in on-policy training; no numbers are stated.

FKIWSV1kSL.one_liner: Benchmark for LLM trading agents that masks identifiers and dates against memorization and decomposes returns with Barra-style attribution.
FKIWSV1kSL.problem: End-to-end LLM trading backtests can overlap with model knowledge cutoffs so memorization replaces reasoning, and raw returns can reflect market beta, style exposure, or regimes rather than stock-selection skill.
FKIWSV1kSL.method: KTD-FIN masks key identifiers and calendar information at the data layer consistently across prompts and tools, and uses a Barra-style performance attribution framework to split portfolio returns into market, style, and stock-selection alpha components.
FKIWSV1kSL.key_idea: Anonymize tickers and dates at the data layer to limit memorized-market retrieval, then attribute returns to market, style, and alpha components.
FKIWSV1kSL.evidence: The visible abstract is cut off before the evaluation; it does not state which agents or periods were tested.

0ixgCzanCD.one_liner: Benchmark of 3,109 questions needing sound plus multiple video streams, with a multi-stream evidence search agent baseline.
0ixgCzanCD.problem: Existing Omni-LLM benchmarks offer limited evaluation of reasoning that requires both sound and complementary information across streams.
0ixgCzanCD.method: MS-OmniBench has twelve subtasks in four families (synchronous cross-stream understanding, asynchronous cross-segment reasoning, audio-anchored retrieval, cross-modal consistency verification) with annotated evidence chains. MESA organizes observations into per-stream event timelines and uses them to guide targeted media inspection.
0ixgCzanCD.key_idea: Build questions whose evidence is spread over camera viewpoints, source-specific audio tracks, and non-adjacent segments, and search them via per-stream event timelines.
0ixgCzanCD.evidence: Evaluates seventeen open-weight and proprietary Omni-LLMs and four existing agentic systems on 3,109 human-reviewed or human-authored questions.
0ixgCzanCD.claimed_gains: Best proprietary and open-weight end-to-end models reach 61.9% and 52.0% accuracy, and the strongest existing agentic system reaches 49.8%; MESA results are cut off in the abstract.

mo6T1hZfAb.one_liner: Proves lower bounds matching the Silver step-size schedule's upper bound for gradient descent, up to polylog factors.
mo6T1hZfAb.problem: It is unclear how much a predefined nonnegative step-size schedule can accelerate gradient descent on L-smooth, mu-strongly convex functions.
mo6T1hZfAb.method: The paper proves lower complexity bounds in both non-anytime and anytime settings, and shows the periodic Silver step-size schedule achieves the anytime upper bound, extending its known bound at completed-block endpoints to every iterate beyond the accuracy threshold. It also derives bounds for the function value gap and squared gradient norm.
mo6T1hZfAb.key_idea: A lower-bound construction against arbitrary step-size schedules, with a silver-ratio exponent, paired with an anytime analysis of the periodic Silver schedule.
mo6T1hZfAb.evidence: Theory only: lower bounds for relative squared distance in non-anytime and anytime settings, plus an anytime upper bound for the Silver schedule; no experiments stated.
mo6T1hZfAb.claimed_gains: Lower bound of order kappa^0.786 (log kappa)^-0.322 log(1/epsilon) versus an anytime upper bound of order kappa^0.786 log(1/epsilon), tight up to polylog(kappa).

ARa9u7Cke7.one_liner: Audits geographic bias in remote-sensing VLMs with pixel-identical location counterfactuals, localizes it by activation patching, and mitigates it by steering.
ARa9u7Cke7.problem: Geographic context can override fixed visual evidence in remote-sensing VLMs, turning a useful prior into a bias that shifts predictions even when the imagery is identical.
ARa9u7Cke7.method: Only the stated location is changed while the image stays fixed; activation patching identifies transformer representations that causally mediate the effect, and bias-weighted steering directions are built for inference-time intervention.
ARa9u7Cke7.key_idea: Steer activations along bias-weighted directions found by activation patching on pixel-identical geographic counterfactuals, without retraining.
ARa9u7Cke7.evidence: Socioeconomic assessment and disaster-damage estimation, using external RWI and damage annotations to judge when shifts are unsupported, with steering tested on unseen images.
ARa9u7Cke7.claimed_gains: Steering consistently reduces geographic counterfactual gaps on unseen images while preserving task-relevant utility; no numbers are stated.

G1fGSMpN6c.one_liner: Uses a discrete diffusion model to generate diverse joint action plans as warm starts for LNS2 in multi-agent path finding.
G1fGSMpN6c.problem: In dense settings, sequential prioritized planning concentrates repeated conflicts on a few agents and hinders local repair, and the initialization stage of repair-based MAPF solvers has received little attention.
G1fGSMpN6c.method: DiffLNS trains a discrete denoising diffusion model (D3PM) with diffusion-aware sparse social attention on expert demonstrations to learn a spatiotemporal prior and sample diverse plans in the categorical action space. These plans warm-start LNS2, which completes unfinished trajectories and resolves conflicts under hard MAPF constraints.
G1fGSMpN6c.key_idea: Sample initial joint plans from a discrete diffusion prior so conflicts are spread more evenly across agents, which makes them easier for LNS2 to repair.
G1fGSMpN6c.evidence: Controlled comparisons of initializations under the same repair procedure and budget, training with at most 96 agents and testing up to 312 agents, and an evaluation across 20 complex and congested scenarios (abstract truncated).
G1fGSMpN6c.claimed_gains: Diffusion-generated initializations reach higher repair success under the same repair procedure and budget despite starting with more colliding pairs, and generalize from at most 96 training agents to tested scenarios with up to 312 agents.

6P6jv40NjZ.one_liner: Maintains a time-indexed belief over moving object locations from timestamped 3D histories to drive a zero-shot VLM navigator.
6P6jv40NjZ.problem: Targets may move while unobserved, so remembered locations are unreliable on arrival, and existing memory retrieval and state prediction do not handle continued hidden world evolution and belief revision under limited visibility.
6P6jv40NjZ.method: EvolvingNav builds a time-indexed belief from timestamped 3D object histories with a persistence-relocation model that keeps probability mass outside the known candidate set. An event-driven filter propagates the belief over time, forecasts occupancy at candidate inspection times and updates on RGB-D evidence, and a frozen zero-shot vision-language controller uses the belief to choose actions.
6P6jv40NjZ.key_idea: Event-driven filtering of a persistence-versus-relocation belief, with visibility-calibrated negative observations and evidence tracking that prevents reusing the same observation.
6P6jv40NjZ.evidence: Not stated; the abstract is truncated before any benchmarks, baselines or results.

AhG6FcJBHt.one_liner: Training-free W4A8 quantization for VLA models using multi-observation activation calibration and exact non-uniform weight codebooks.
AhG6FcJBHt.problem: Under W4A8 post-training quantization, static 4-bit weight errors recur at every denoising step and compound across consecutive requests, while activation channel peaks drift across denoising steps and observations.
AhG6FcJBHt.method: RMAEC records per-channel token percentiles at every denoising step, aggregates their maxima within each request and across diverse observations, and freezes the resulting scales. Exact non-uniform codebook construction aggregates repeated weight values to make dynamic programming tractable at layer scale, giving globally optimal levels for fixed row scales.
AhG6FcJBHt.key_idea: Calibrate activation scales to extremes over both denoising steps and observations, and solve for optimal non-uniform weight levels exactly by dynamic programming over aggregated repeated values.
AhG6FcJBHt.evidence: An extreme-value model predicts that the calibration scales grow sub-linearly with the number of observations; experimental results are not visible in the truncated abstract.

ttj5xR0Agb.one_liner: Derives open-vocabulary mutual information (OVMI) to compare speech BCIs on one common reference scale.
ttj5xR0Agb.problem: Speech BCI scores are rarely comparable because systems differ in datasets, recording methods, speech types and vocabularies, and metrics computed only over supported words can overstate how much intended speech is communicated.
ttj5xR0Agb.method: Derives OVMI, an information-theoretic quantity that measures the information a decoder conveys relative to a reference distribution over the words a user may wish to communicate. Uses it to compare existing systems and expose trade-offs between how much of the user's language a system supports and how accurately it decodes it.
ttj5xR0Agb.key_idea: Measure decoder output as mutual information relative to a fixed reference word distribution, so supported-vocabulary size is accounted for in the score.
ttj5xR0Agb.evidence: Applied to compare existing speech BCI systems, showing that accuracy, word error rate and other metrics over supported words alone can overstate communication.

qY0WTSkFj9.one_liner: Proves uniform-random interpolating ReLU parameters generalize at rate O~(wdWD/n) when a smaller w-by-d network explains the data.
qY0WTSkFj9.problem: Generalization of a randomly drawn interpolating ReLU network is normally governed by the VC dimension of the full W-by-D class, ignoring that the data may be explained by a smaller network.
qY0WTSkFj9.method: Draws parameters uniformly at random from those that interpolate the data in a width-W depth-D ReLU architecture with weights bounded in [-M, M]. A proof technique called deep lifting constructs an exponential volume of near-equivalent W-by-D parameters around the small w-by-d witness and ties that volume to its stability properties.
qY0WTSkFj9.key_idea: A small w-by-d interpolating network witnesses an exponential volume of W-by-D interpolating parameters, which outweighs the volume of poorly generalizing ones.
qY0WTSkFj9.evidence: Theoretical bounds, examples converting approximation-theoretic results into generalization guarantees for nonparametric classes, and an extension showing generalization can survive label corruptions.
qY0WTSkFj9.claimed_gains: Generalization at rate O~(wdWD/n) rather than a rate governed by the VC dimension of the full W-by-D hypothesis class.

rmbw0iDAnI.one_liner: Sample complexity bounds for language generation in the limit under noise, prompting, and feedback across several language classes.
rmbw0iDAnI.problem: How many examples a learner needs to generate unseen strings in the limit has not been studied under noisy input, prefix conditioning, and feedback.
rmbw0iDAnI.method: They analyze sample complexity for partially-ordered (PO) languages, a class not previously analyzed in this framework, giving exponential upper and lower bounds, show that context-free sample bounds remain uncomputable in every setting, and quantify the effect of finite noise, prompting, and finite feedback for regular, LTT, and PO languages.
rmbw0iDAnI.key_idea: Analyze generation-in-the-limit sample complexity per language class (regular, LTT, PO, context-free) and compare each noise, prompting, and feedback extension against the base bound.
rmbw0iDAnI.evidence: Theoretical upper and lower bounds and an uncomputability result; no experiments are stated.
rmbw0iDAnI.claimed_gains: Finite noise adds only a linear additive term to the sample complexity, prompting generally leaves the bounds unchanged, and finite feedback can sometimes reduce them exponentially.

vRPakFUfgS.one_liner: Shares all Gaussian attributes across LoD levels except scale and opacity, which get compact per-level residual offsets, plus codebook compression.
vRPakFUfgS.problem: LoD for 3DGS faces a trade-off: separate Gaussian sets per level inflate resident memory, while a single shared set degrades quality, so large scenes run out of memory or render slowly on constrained devices.
vRPakFUfgS.method: SAS-LoD keeps one base Gaussian set with compact level-wise residual offsets for scale and opacity (4 of 59 parameters), shares all other attributes, and adds codebook compression with on-demand decoding.
vRPakFUfgS.key_idea: Only scale and opacity adapt Gaussian footprints across LoD levels, so store them as per-level residuals over one shared Gaussian set and share the remaining attributes.
vRPakFUfgS.evidence: The abstract states the observation that scale and opacity account for 4 of 59 parameters, but names no datasets or measurements.

MU3zPRfKjc.one_liner: Diffusion SBI with an observation-count-aware diffusion coefficient, hierarchical blockwise sampling, and path-regularized fine-tuning for misspecified simulators.
MU3zPRfKjc.problem: Simulation-based inference is hard when many heterogeneous observations must be composed, hierarchical latent structure must be preserved, and the simulator is misspecified relative to observed data.
MU3zPRfKjc.method: They extend compositional score-based inference with a continuous-time diffusion coefficient that accounts for the number of observations, and introduce Hierarchical Blockwise Diffusion Sampling (HBDS) to infer shared parameters and group-specific latent states from one pretrained model with the hierarchy set only at sampling time. Path-regularized fine-tuning adapts the learned likelihood to observations, and Girsanov's theorem quantifies path divergence between pretrained and fine-tuned models to judge whether a misspecification correction is needed.
MU3zPRfKjc.key_idea: Scale the diffusion coefficient by the number of observations to compose scores without Jacobian corrections, set hierarchy only at sampling time, and fine-tune with a path-divergence regularizer.
MU3zPRfKjc.evidence: Compositional sampling on exact-score Gaussian and SLCP benchmarks; the rest of the evaluation is cut off in the abstract.

4lMpdQ0xnO.one_liner: Expresses vision tasks as native text and image generation in one unified multimodal model trained on a converted instruction corpus.
4lMpdQ0xnO.problem: Heterogeneous computer vision tasks usually need task-specific architectures or prediction heads rather than one model working through native generation spaces.
4lMpdQ0xnO.method: VisionUMM starts from an off-the-shelf pretrained unified multimodal model and is trained mainly on VisionCorpus, built by converting heterogeneous vision annotations into instruction-response examples with text, image, or mixed targets. Natural-language instructions and optional visual prompts specify the task, target regions or views, and decoding convention, with text outputs for symbolic records and images for dense targets.
4lMpdQ0xnO.key_idea: Convert every vision annotation into an instruction-response pair whose answer is text, an image, or both, so one pretrained unified multimodal model handles all tasks without heads.
4lMpdQ0xnO.evidence: Structured visual understanding, dense geometric prediction, segmentation, and multi-view geometry, covering detection, OCR, keypoints, segmentation, depth, surface normals, point maps, and camera pose estimation.
4lMpdQ0xnO.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract only claims competitive results across structured visual understanding, dense geometric prediction, segmentation, and multi-view visual geometry.

uuBFhjgZ4j.one_liner: Adaptive pruning for irregular multivariate time series where one shared variation signal drives multiple pruning decisions via learnable calibrators.
uuBFhjgZ4j.problem: Redundant historical segments distract attention in irregular multivariate time series forecasting, and existing pruning methods use independently designed rules per component that can conflict on the same sample.
uuBFhjgZ4j.method: ADDP summarizes each sample's historical variation in a shared signal, and lightweight learnable calibrators use it to set segment redundancy, the shared information between aggressive and conservative pruning views, and the view weights. It builds the two complementary views and jointly trains a shared forecasting model.
uuBFhjgZ4j.key_idea: Derive one shared continuous volatility signal per sample that controls segment pruning, view overlap, and view weighting through learnable calibrators.
uuBFhjgZ4j.evidence: Experiments on PhysioNet, Activity, USHCN, and MIMIC-III against competing methods including Hi-Patch.
uuBFhjgZ4j.claimed_gains: Lowest mean MSE on each of four datasets; on MIMIC-III, MSE is reduced by 5.05% relative to Hi-Patch, the strongest baseline.

fHnt37QnF2.one_liner: Constructs POMDP pairs showing off-policy evaluation under history-dependent logging needs exponential samples despite bounded coverage and revealing.
fHnt37QnF2.problem: Multi-step revealing makes off-policy evaluation tractable under memoryless logging, but it is unclear whether this holds when the logger depends on history.
fHnt37QnF2.method: For every horizon H>=3 they build two realizable POMDPs with four actions, at most four states per layer, a known logger, and a memoryless target. They also give a finite-class OPE guarantee under action and history coverage using common observable value representations.
fHnt37QnF2.key_idea: Logger memory makes states distinguishable while reset erases the model-distinguishing evidence the target preserves, so the logged laws become exponentially close.
fHnt37QnF2.evidence: Theoretical constructions and proofs in the visible abstract: a lower bound for every H>=3, a common-operator variant, a finite-class OPE guarantee, and matching passive and budgeted readout rates on a four-action continuum.
fHnt37QnF2.claimed_gains: Target values differ by 1/2 while the KL divergence between the logged laws is Theta(4^-(H-1)), forcing exponential sample complexity.

6lVZYaXpH6.one_liner: Synthesizes retraining-like output targets for forget samples from the original model alone, then distills an unlearned model on forget data.
6lVZYaXpH6.problem: Unlearning is evaluated against a retrained oracle, but when retain data are unavailable it is unclear whether the retrained model's outputs on forget samples can be approximated from the original model and forget data alone.
6lVZYaXpH6.method: Studies the original-to-retrained output change through four questions (which forget samples change argmax, which class loses mass, how much, where it is redistributed), builds synthetic retrained targets from the observed patterns, and distills an unlearned model directly on forget data.
6lVZYaXpH6.key_idea: Predict how a retrained model shifts probability mass on forget samples (uncertainty-driven argmax change, loss from the top-1 class, gain for high-ranked alternatives) and distill toward those synthetic targets.
6lVZYaXpH6.evidence: Food-101, Oxford Pets, Stanford Cars, CIFAR-100, and Tiny-ImageNet with ResNet-18, DeiT-T, and ViT-S, in forget-only regimes with different fractions of removed samples.
6lVZYaXpH6.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract is truncated after saying the distilled model achieves a favorable tradeoff between forgetting, utility, and a cut-off third criterion.

7YfXUOMINd.one_liner: MacroData: 400K multi-reference image generation samples with up to 10 references each, plus the 4,000-sample MacroBench.
7YfXUOMINd.problem: Multi-reference image generation models degrade severely as the number of references grows because existing datasets are dominated by single- or few-reference pairs and lack structured long-context supervision, and standardized evaluation protocols are missing.
7YfXUOMINd.method: MacroData organizes samples across four dimensions (Customization, Illustration, Spatial reasoning, Temporal dynamics), each with up to 10 reference images. MacroBench assesses generative coherence across graded task dimensions and input scales, and models are fine-tuned on MacroData.
7YfXUOMINd.key_idea: Supply structured long-context supervision with up to 10 references per sample across four complementary task dimensions, instead of changing the model.
7YfXUOMINd.evidence: Fine-tuning on MacroData evaluated on MacroBench, with ablations on cross-task co-training and strategies for long-context complexity.
7YfXUOMINd.claimed_gains: Fine-tuning on MacroData yields substantial improvements in multi-reference generation; no numeric results are stated in the abstract.

h0aSMOkfhu.one_liner: Agentic framework that builds video-language judge benchmarks over 100-hour playlists with causally degraded answer pairs, no human annotation.
h0aSMOkfhu.problem: It is unknown whether video-language judges stay reliable when evidence is buried in day-long videos, and existing benchmarks use short videos, answer pairs separable from the transcript, and costly human labels.
h0aSMOkfhu.method: PlaylistEval automatically generates questions with paired answers whose differences are controlled by causal degradation, so every pair requires retrieval across the collection. The benchmark spans seven domains of static and dynamic knowledge over 100-hour playlist collections.
h0aSMOkfhu.key_idea: Create answer pairs by controlled causal degradation of a correct answer so judging each pair demands retrieval across a very long video collection.
h0aSMOkfhu.evidence: 630 pairs across seven domains, validated against humans on a stratified 152-pair subset, with 17 omnimodal and multimodal models from eight families evaluated.
h0aSMOkfhu.claimed_gains: The benchmark has 630 pairs and agrees with human judgments 93.0% of the time on a stratified subset of 152 pairs (IAA 0.781), and frontier judges reach only 75.4% pairwise accuracy.

z6CebbSH73.one_liner: Fits compute-optimal scaling laws for text-to-image diffusion using Abra flow-matching transformers trained from 10^19 to 10^22 FLOPs.
z6CebbSH73.problem: Compute-optimal scaling laws guide frontier language model training but remain largely unexplored for visual generation.
z6CebbSH73.method: The authors train Abra, a controlled family of flow-matching transformers, across three orders of magnitude of compute and fit scaling laws to loss. They then check whether the same predictability holds for generative quality metrics, optimal CFG settings, representation quality and training-curve shape.
z6CebbSH73.key_idea: Fit compute-optimal loss laws on a controlled flow-matching transformer family over a wide compute grid, then extend the fits to quality metrics, CFG and training-curve shape.
z6CebbSH73.evidence: Abra family of text-to-image flow-matching transformers trained from 10^19 to 10^22 FLOPs, larger budgets than previous works.
z6CebbSH73.claimed_gains: Compute optimality occurs at approximately 200 image tokens per parameter, ten times the Chinchilla prescription for LLMs, and diffusion models are robust to overtraining.

JPPvmnym2h.one_liner: Training-free diffusion-transformer acceleration that predicts skipped solver outputs from the latest exact output plus a geometrically retained innovation fraction.
JPPvmnym2h.problem: Diffusion transformers incur high inference cost from repeated model evaluations along a sampling trajectory.
JPPvmnym2h.method: GeoShrink keeps the original solver grid and evaluates the model only at a prescribed set of anchors; at skipped stages it adds a geometrically retained fraction of the latest observed innovation to the most recent exact output. The rule is derived from chordal tangent transport and round-trip line projection, with an anchor-spacing principle that minimizes the largest adjacent gap expansion.
JPPvmnym2h.key_idea: At skipped steps, add a geometrically shrunk fraction of the latest observed innovation to the last exact model output, with anchors spaced to minimize the largest adjacent gap expansion.
JPPvmnym2h.evidence: Experiments cover image, video, motion and audio generation plus adapted 3D backends, including FLUX and HunyuanVideo, with fixed-evaluation-budget comparisons.
JPPvmnym2h.claimed_gains: At about 5x acceleration, FLUX PSNR improves by 3.10 dB over the strongest listed baseline; on HunyuanVideo it reports a 4.99x speedup and +5.44 dB ChronoMagic-Bench-150 PSNR over the strongest listed fidelity baseline.

g63ZacFUUV.one_liner: Co-trains query-side and item-side LLM keyword generators with alternating reinforcement learning against each other's frozen index.
g63ZacFUUV.problem: Existing LLM retrieval methods adapt only the query side and leave item representations fixed, which limits mutual alignment and retrieval performance.
g63ZacFUUV.method: Supervised fine-tuning builds an aligned keyword space, then each generator is trained by RL against the opposite side's frozen index. Both sides optimize a query-to-item F1 objective; the item side gets a counterfactual marginal reward for each item's impact.
g63ZacFUUV.key_idea: Alternately train query and item keyword generators with RL on a shared F1 objective, giving items a counterfactual marginal reward that isolates each item's retrieval impact.
g63ZacFUUV.evidence: Comparison against 10 sparse, dense and generative retrieval baselines on an internal APP Marketplace dataset and the public WANDS benchmark, plus analysis of co-evolution dynamics.
g63ZacFUUV.claimed_gains: Improves F1 over the strongest baseline by 10.9% on the internal APP Marketplace dataset and 36.1% on WANDS.

YXeYwb5EYf.one_liner: Adds a contact-aware hybrid state to a streaming audio-visual generator so sound onsets stay aligned with rigid-body contacts.
YXeYwb5EYf.problem: Under chunk-wise autoregressive rollout, motion errors accumulate (contact-phase drift) and produce delayed, missing, or spurious audio events.
YXeYwb5EYf.method: Tora-live augments a few-step chunk-causal generator with a hybrid state of dominant-object kinematics and explicit contact-phase variables, maintained online by state propagation and closed-loop correction from generated video. The state conditions both modalities, and a contact-focused rollout objective aligns audio onsets with scheduled contacts.
YXeYwb5EYf.key_idea: Maintain an online hybrid state of object kinematics and contact-phase variables, corrected from generated video, and condition both audio and video on it.
YXeYwb5EYf.evidence: Evaluated on ContactBench, a benchmark the authors build for contact-dominated rigid-body scenes (details truncated in the abstract).

LzZW4KnC2Y.one_liner: Optimizes latent states inserted at a Transformer layer using reward-weighted gradients flowing through causal self-attention from the generated continuation.
LzZW4KnC2Y.problem: Existing optimization-based latent reasoning links latent states to the reasoning trajectory through decoded tokens, making credit assignment indirect and opaque.
LzZW4KnC2Y.method: GradCuit inserts optimizable latent states at a chosen layer between prompt and continuation hidden states, with model parameters frozen. Causal self-attention gives every continuation-token log-probability a differentiable path to each latent, so reward-weighted gradients assign credit directly to the latents.
LzZW4KnC2Y.key_idea: Insert latent states mid-network and backpropagate reward-weighted continuation log-probabilities to them through self-attention, bypassing decoded-token credit assignment.
LzZW4KnC2Y.evidence: Five instruction-tuned backbones, three reasoning benchmarks and two answer formats, with a sweep over seven learning rates compared against LatentSeek.
LzZW4KnC2Y.claimed_gains: Average accuracy of 64.5%, 6.6 percentage points above chain-of-thought prompting and 2.4 points above the strongest competing method; accuracy standard deviation across seven learning rates falls from 1.53 to 0.82 relative to LatentSeek.

2S9TOnFTBZ.one_liner: Unified video context-dependent concept segmentation using an evolving concept discriminative subspace and temporal clip balancing.
2S9TOnFTBZ.problem: Video context-dependent concept segmentation across natural, medical, and 3D medical scenarios must handle concepts whose discriminative evidence drifts with visual context, plus severe cross-task imbalance in video and frame counts.
2S9TOnFTBZ.method: EvoCDS builds an evolving concept discriminative subspace that preserves reliable historical directions while adapting to current evidence, motivated by the compact low-dimensional structure of concept-specific discriminative information. Temporal clip balancing stabilizes joint learning across heterogeneous sequence datasets.
2S9TOnFTBZ.key_idea: Maintain a low-dimensional discriminative subspace per concept that keeps reliable past directions and updates with current evidence to track concept drift.
2S9TOnFTBZ.evidence: Eight tasks spanning natural and medical scenarios compared with unified models and specialized methods, plus the new Video-CD benchmark of 201 videos and 34,562 frames for concept drift.
2S9TOnFTBZ.claimed_gains: not stated numerically; the abstract reports consistent gains over existing unified models and competitive performance against specialized methods across eight tasks.

gjuEk72u4p.one_liner: Proves activation patching evidence can leave exponentially many minimum faithful circuits indistinguishable in additive models, with matching bounds.
gjuEk72u4p.problem: Activation patching can establish circuit faithfulness without determining a unique minimum circuit.
gjuEk72u4p.method: For additive n-component models with minimum r-faithful cardinality k, they prove complete order-r evidence admits at most binom(n-1,k) minimum circuits, give a patched ReLU construction that attains the bound, and show robustness results and an extremal query lower bound.
gjuEk72u4p.key_idea: Extremal combinatorics: low-order patching responses cannot distinguish minimum faithful circuits, and a patched ReLU model with m patching sites attains the binomial bound.
gjuEk72u4p.evidence: Theoretical proofs and explicit extremal constructions for additive models; no empirical experiments are stated.
gjuEk72u4p.claimed_gains: not stated numerically; the extremal count of minimum circuits grows exponentially in n, roughly 2^n up to lower-order factors at k = ceil(n/2).

asi6qPhqU5.one_liner: Conditions generation on a noisy semantic representation so posteriors act as exponential tilts by linear-quadratic rewards.
asi6qPhqU5.problem: Steering a generative model toward a property usually needs separate fine-tuning per reward or extra computation during sampling.
asi6qPhqU5.method: Semantic noising conditions generation on a noisy semantic representation of the data; the resulting posteriors correspond to exponential tilts by linear-quadratic rewards in semantic space, so objectives and strengths can be chosen after training. A conditional generator can approximate them directly, and diffusion models over semantic representations give analytic tilted denoisers.
asi6qPhqU5.key_idea: Noising the semantic representation makes conditional posteriors equal exponential tilts by linear-quadratic rewards, so reward choice and strength can be set after training.
asi6qPhqU5.evidence: Three settings: MolGPT autoregressive molecular generation with linear property predictors, a joint image and CLIP-embedding diffusion model on ImageNet compared with REG, and pretrained factorized models such as Kandinsky.
asi6qPhqU5.claimed_gains: not stated numerically; the abstract reports a better reward-KL trade-off than separately trained property-conditioned models and FID comparable to REG on ImageNet.

qA7w8uFhQO.one_liner: Reuses rollout computation graphs and activations for the policy update in diffusion RL, removing redundant timestep recomputation.
qA7w8uFhQO.problem: Diffusion RL methods such as DanceGRPO and FlowGRPO recompute selected timesteps with gradient tracking after rollout, which is redundant under on-policy training with the same backend.
qA7w8uFhQO.method: LeanGRPO restructures the data-parallel layout and adds two recompute-free schedules: Retain enables gradient tracking during rollout and reuses computation graphs and saved activations for backward, while Reweight backpropagates each selected step with a provisional advantage, delays gradient synchronization, and corrects with the true advantage after the trajectory completes.
qA7w8uFhQO.key_idea: Track gradients during rollout and either keep the graph (Retain) or backpropagate with a provisional advantage then correct it (Reweight), so no timestep is recomputed.
qA7w8uFhQO.evidence: FlowGRPO and DanceGRPO with FLUX.1-dev and Wan; the abstract is truncated before the remaining results.
qA7w8uFhQO.claimed_gains: Up to 1.83x end-to-end speedup while preserving the original optimization objective.

1tSzuym019.one_liner: Pipeline-parallel training that sparsifies activations per input on the critical path and sends residuals asynchronously during idle windows.
1tSzuym019.problem: Inter-stage communication bottlenecks pipeline parallelism on low-bandwidth networks, and existing extreme compression projects activations into a static, data-oblivious subspace that restricts capacity and starves orthogonal dimensions of gradient updates.
1tSzuym019.method: CoverPipe uses input-adaptive sparsification to preserve salient features per sample on the critical path, and asynchronously transmits the residual components during idle communication windows to restore full representational capacity and gradient flow.
1tSzuym019.key_idea: Input-adaptive sparsification of latent vectors on the critical path, with residuals overlapped with computation, instead of fixed data-oblivious projections.
1tSzuym019.evidence: A unified analytical framework showing fixed projections impair trainability, plus evaluations on standard and MoE Transformer workloads across 60-500 Mbps networks and under Chinchilla-optimal training budgets.
1tSzuym019.claimed_gains: not stated numerically; the abstract says CoverPipe outperforms uncompressed and compressed baselines in wall-clock convergence while maintaining high throughput.

arzcZjJl7a.one_liner: Continual model editing of MLLM visual encoders for new corruptions, with quality-weighted key-value pairs and a principal component constraint.
arzcZjJl7a.problem: Robust MLLMs are optimized for predefined corruptions and generalize poorly to unknown ones, while adapting to new corruptions causes catastrophic forgetting of earlier robustness.
arzcZjJl7a.method: They fine-tune the visual encoder with an additional robustness loss to obtain corrupted key-value pairs, use a dynamic key-value construction strategy that weights samples by quality for limited-data updates, and add a principal component constraint on parameter updates to mitigate forgetting. They also introduce VCBench, covering vision questions under 17 common real-world visual corruptions.
arzcZjJl7a.key_idea: Edit the visual encoder using quality-weighted corrupted key-value pairs while constraining updates by principal components to preserve pretrained knowledge.
arzcZjJl7a.evidence: VCBench (17 corruption types) and multiple benchmarks; the abstract is truncated before the results.

Xbzuq2Guj0.one_liner: Backpropagates a differentiable pairwise comparison against a peer image from the current model instead of a pointwise reward.
Xbzuq2Guj0.problem: Reward feedback learning for text-to-image models is prone to reward hacking, since maximizing a per-image reward score can amplify patterns like oversaturated colors without improving perceived quality.
Xbzuq2Guj0.method: PairReFL replaces scalar-score maximization with a differentiable comparison against another image sampled from the current model, so the reference changes as the model learns. It relies on a differentiable pairwise reward model.
Xbzuq2Guj0.key_idea: Compare each generated image to a peer sampled from the current model with a differentiable pairwise reward model, so the reference moves with the policy.
Xbzuq2Guj0.evidence: Four human-preference metrics compared against pointwise reward feedback learning and policy-gradient baselines, plus a comparison of pairwise versus pointwise reward-model error on visual-quality comparisons.
Xbzuq2Guj0.claimed_gains: PairReFL outperforms pointwise reward feedback learning by up to 1.1% and the strongest policy-gradient baseline by up to 3.7%, and the pairwise reward model reduces the error rate in visual-quality comparisons by 62% relative to its pointwise counterpart.

T1Amk2fx4r.one_liner: Benchmark evaluating whether AI agents propose mechanistic hypotheses from empirical data with known generating mechanisms.
T1Amk2fx4r.problem: AI agents increasingly support scientific data analysis, but their ability to turn empirical findings into mechanistic hypotheses is insufficiently examined.
T1Amk2fx4r.method: MechHypoBench combines paper-derived mechanisms from 14 scientific fields with independently collected datasets totaling 17.98 million records, aligning by experimental semantic roles so mechanisms generate responses under empirically derived conditions as anonymized tasks. Agents propose open-form hypotheses, which are scored by their consequences under withheld conditions.
T1Amk2fx4r.key_idea: Score open-form mechanistic hypotheses by their predicted consequences under withheld conditions, on tasks generated from a known mechanism over real data.
T1Amk2fx4r.evidence: Experiments with general agents and AI scientists on the benchmark.
T1Amk2fx4r.claimed_gains: not stated numerically; the abstract reports a substantial gap between generated hypotheses and the underlying mechanisms.

xK7H5r3Rx5.one_liner: Masked feature prediction where an independently encoded source image helps predict video targets conditioned on the signed time interval.
xK7H5r3Rx5.problem: Image self-supervision learns spatial structure from one moment and video methods learn temporal relations inside jointly computed representations, so it is unclear whether watching change can improve features available from a single image.
xK7H5r3Rx5.method: W2Rep uses a predictor conditioned on visible video context, the queried location, and the signed time interval to predict features at a target moment from an independently encoded source image at the same or another moment.
xK7H5r3Rx5.key_idea: Predict masked features at another moment from a separately encoded source image plus video context and signed time offset, so cross-frame prediction updates the image features directly.
xK7H5r3Rx5.evidence: Frozen and fine-tuned recognition across model scales and downstream tasks under their comparison protocol, with controlled experiments on source-image updates, video context, and temporal displacement.
xK7H5r3Rx5.claimed_gains: not stated numerically; the abstract reports improved frozen and fine-tuned recognition, with joint video encoding giving further gains over frame-wise aggregation.

9IrVsGwao9.one_liner: Uses OCR as training-only supervision so OCR-free KIE predicts fixed-length latent evidence tokens before generating answers.
9IrVsGwao9.problem: OCR-free KIE models learn text-location associations implicitly from answer supervision, while OCR-augmented methods need external OCR and variable-length context at inference.
9IrVsGwao9.method: LAYER predicts a fixed-length sequence of continuous visual latent tokens in parallel from a document image and field query, and the language model then conditions on them plus the image-query context to generate structured answers. Layout-aware Feature Alignment and Confidence-Gated Contrastive Learning supervise the latents with OCR in a two-stage training scheme, so inference needs only the image and query.
9IrVsGwao9.key_idea: Align predicted latent tokens to visual features of OCR text rendered in page layout, and contrast answer values with supporting OCR blocks, using OCR only during training.
9IrVsGwao9.evidence: Experiments on public KIE benchmarks reporting pooled micro-F1 gains (the abstract is truncated before the numbers).

GtGzgx41RQ.one_liner: Precomputes outputs for fixed basis vectors at each state update, then reconstructs decode reads from a compact sketch.
GtGzgx41RQ.problem: In hybrid linear-attention decoding, every new query needs a full recurrent-state read even though the state is unchanged between buffered updates, making state access a bottleneck at large decode batches.
GtGzgx41RQ.method: At each state update, SketchSSM reads the full state once to precompute outputs for offline-fixed basis vectors and stores them as a compact sketch. Each later decode step combines the sketch vectors with query-dependent coefficients to reconstruct the output without a full-state read.
GtGzgx41RQ.key_idea: Approximate the state read with a low-rank, state-weighted query approximation using offline-fixed basis vectors whose outputs are precomputed once per state update.
GtGzgx41RQ.evidence: Evaluated on four Mamba-2-, GDN-, and KDA-based models across four long-generation reasoning benchmarks and four RULER retrieval tasks, with kernel timing on one NVIDIA B300 against a Standard vLLM baseline.
GtGzgx41RQ.claimed_gains: At a mean sketch rank of 8, state-access traffic drops by approximately 10x while matching the average accuracy of the FP32 full-state baseline; the kernel speedup figure over Standard vLLM is cut off in the abstract.

rQZIZfKRfg.one_liner: Selects egocentric human clips for each robot demonstration via a recall-ranking-re-ranking cascade, treating data selection as recommendation.
rQZIZfKRfg.problem: It is unclear which of the scaled-up egocentric human videos actually benefit dexterous manipulation.
rQZIZfKRfg.method: SiMDex casts human data selection for VLA post-training as a recommendation problem. For each robot demonstration, recall and ranking stages pick a task-relevant subset from about 32M egocentric samples in a morphology-agnostic action space, and re-ranking verifies it on pixels, with no change to VLA architecture or training.
rQZIZfKRfg.key_idea: A recall-ranking-re-ranking cascade retrieves human clips in a morphology-agnostic action space, then verifies them on pixels.
rQZIZfKRfg.evidence: Compared against a baseline trained with an equal amount of randomly sampled human data, mining from a pool of about 32M egocentric human samples for VLA post-training in dexterous manipulation.
rQZIZfKRfg.claimed_gains: Using only about 1.49M mined samples (<5% of the pool), overall success rate improves from 47.7% to 61.7%.

peGRILBOdk.one_liner: Activates 4D spherical-harmonic bands per Gaussian only when a joint update lowers loss on disjoint observation sets.
peGRILBOdk.problem: Giving every Gaussian a full angular-temporal basis spends storage and computation on capacity with little reconstruction benefit, and cheap cues such as motion or residual magnitude are only indirect indicators of need.
peGRILBOdk.method: Starting from base color, OccamSplat probes candidate 4DSH bands with zero coefficients, which preserves the current rendering. Cross-observation gradient agreement yields bounded coefficient updates, accepted only when joint rendering reduces the loss on two disjoint sampled observation sets not used to construct them.
peGRILBOdk.key_idea: Verify the rendering benefit of a concrete joint 4DSH coefficient update on disjoint observation sets before activating appearance capacity.
peGRILBOdk.evidence: Evaluated on Neural 3D Video, MeetRoom, and Technicolor light-field, with the headline comparison on Neural 3D Video against Uniform 4DSH under the same backbone and densification configuration.
peGRILBOdk.claimed_gains: On Neural 3D Video, PSNR improves by 0.60 dB over Uniform 4DSH with 12.8% of non-DC coefficient rows active, while rendering at 257 FPS.

gaT30XQX4s.one_liner: Proves matching bounds linking expected-regret budget to pseudo-regret tail probability in heavy-tailed bandits, and gives the BCRR algorithm.
gaT30XQX4s.problem: Low expected regret can hide large regret on individual runs, and under heavy-tailed rewards extreme observations distort reward estimates.
gaT30XQX4s.method: Under a known bound on the centered (1+epsilon)-th moment, the authors establish matching upper and lower bounds relating a worst-case expected-regret budget to the pseudo-regret tail probability. They propose Budget-Calibrated Robust Racing (BCRR), which jointly calibrates exploration and robust arm elimination to the expected-regret budget.
gaT30XQX4s.key_idea: Calibrate exploration and robust arm elimination to a given expected-regret budget, trading average performance for tail protection.
gaT30XQX4s.evidence: Matching upper and lower bounds under a known (1+epsilon)-th centered moment bound, plus numerical experiments whose details are cut off in the abstract.
gaT30XQX4s.claimed_gains: For fixed epsilon and a fixed number of arms, a budget of order rho times the minimax regret scale yields a rho-fold improvement in the negative-log tail rate, up to constants.

zR8nHrzl1K.one_liner: Surrogate-Profit UCB learns context-dependent price and stock levels from censored sales using data from similar past market contexts.
zR8nHrzl1K.problem: When a product sells out, the seller sees only units sold, not unmet demand, so a context-dependent pricing and stocking policy must be learned without a parametric demand model or fully observed profit.
zR8nHrzl1K.method: SP-UCB turns each incomplete sales record into a surrogate-profit guide for both inventory and price decisions, using data from past rounds with similar market conditions. It learns while serving customers, with no separate exploration phase and no need to recover all demand hidden by stockouts.
zR8nHrzl1K.key_idea: Build a surrogate-profit upper confidence bound from censored sales in rounds with similar contexts to guide joint price and inventory decisions.
zR8nHrzl1K.evidence: A proof of minimax optimality, with strictly faster rates when expected profit varies more smoothly with price, plus numerical experiments whose details are not given.

Mi4oZjL5uD.one_liner: Learnable neural attenuation models underwater particle effects; a generative prior refines coarse Gaussians into texture Gaussians.
Mi4oZjL5uD.problem: Existing underwater Gaussian splatting uses particle-specific modeling that adapts poorly across static, dynamic, and uncertain-scattering scenes, and underwater attenuation worsens the low-frequency bias of 3D Gaussians, hurting local high-frequency textures.
Mi4oZjL5uD.method: Adaptive Particle Modeling uses a learnable neural attenuation function to estimate depth-dependent absorption and scattering terms. Progressive Gaussian Generation uses optimized coarse Gaussians to generate fine-grained texture Gaussians guided by a generative prior.
Mi4oZjL5uD.key_idea: Estimate depth-dependent absorption and scattering with a learnable neural attenuation function, and generate fine texture Gaussians from coarse Gaussians under a generative prior.
Mi4oZjL5uD.evidence: The abstract says extensive experiments were run, but datasets, baselines, and metrics are cut off.

YAV7X1GQDH.one_liner: Generates four sparse, jointly consistent high-resolution panoramas at selected poses from one panorama, then reconstructs a 3D world.
YAV7X1GQDH.problem: Single-panorama 3D world construction leaves large regions unobserved, and dense panoramic-video expansion is redundant, accumulates error over long trajectories, and can give inconsistent directions.
YAV7X1GQDH.method: Coverage-Guided View Selection picks target locations using scene-adaptive quadrants and warp-based coverage scores. Joint Panoramic Diffusion uses Gaussian-splatting-based geometric warps to jointly synthesize four pose-grounded, cross-view-consistent panoramas, which feed an existing reconstruction pipeline.
YAV7X1GQDH.key_idea: Select informative target views by warp-based coverage, then jointly diffuse four warp-conditioned panoramas with global attention kept only in sensitive layers.
YAV7X1GQDH.evidence: The abstract states that experiments were run, but datasets, baselines, and metrics are cut off.

4bCRO5OIWY.one_liner: Trains a Supervisor with a flow-matching loss to sample orchestration strategies by reward and evolve a skill library recursively.
4bCRO5OIWY.problem: Orchestration methods suffer strategy collapse under reward maximization, high gradient variance with opaque credit assignment, and skill evolution decided by prompting an LLM rather than by training signals.
4bCRO5OIWY.method: A trainable Supervisor interacts over multiple turns with an environment holding a dynamic skill library and a frozen executor. Tempered Trajectory Balance (TTB), a regression-based flow-matching loss, samples strategies in proportion to reward, and a jointly learned backward policy gives per-step credit assignment that drives a recursive skill evolution mechanism.
4bCRO5OIWY.key_idea: Tempered Trajectory Balance samples orchestration strategies proportional to reward, and its flow diagnostics decide when, what, and where to evolve skills.
4bCRO5OIWY.evidence: Experiments on 14 datasets; the specific results are cut off in the abstract.

I1RvKeAgPO.one_liner: Splits RL credit into reasoning-trajectory ranking credit and target-path credit over hierarchical Semantic ID decisions for generative recommendation.
I1RvKeAgPO.problem: Sequence-level RL broadcasts one outcome advantage to all tokens, so for hierarchical Semantic IDs incorrect suffix decisions can be reinforced while correct prefix decisions are suppressed.
I1RvKeAgPO.method: DG-HCA grounds policy optimization in retrieval feedback from Constrained Beam Search. Ranking-Driven Reasoning Credit scores reasoning trajectories by retrieval quality, Target-Path SID Credit assigns relative credit over hierarchical decisions along the ground-truth path, and Target-Path Recovery adds supervision when beam search deviates from the target SID.
I1RvKeAgPO.key_idea: Assign credit at both the trajectory level (retrieval quality) and per-level SID actions along the ground-truth path, instead of one broadcast sequence advantage.
I1RvKeAgPO.evidence: Experiments on three public Amazon datasets, with ablations on SID-level credit assignment and Target-Path Recovery.
I1RvKeAgPO.claimed_gains: Competitive recommendation performance and the best NDCG@10 on all three datasets; no numeric values are stated.

tzEomMtqDX.one_liner: Plug-in that refines pretrained PDE surrogates with a flow-matching residual model, then aligns rollouts with trajectory-level RL rewards.
tzEomMtqDX.problem: MSE-trained PDE surrogates lose high-frequency, fine-scale structure, while generative models accumulate stochastic errors in autoregressive rollouts and lose long-term stability.
tzEomMtqDX.method: In the refinement stage, a conditional flow-matching model learns the residual distribution around the deterministic base prediction. In the alignment stage, multiple trajectories are generated from the same input and the refiner is reinforced with trajectory-level rewards for long-horizon dynamical alignment.
tzEomMtqDX.key_idea: A flow-matching refiner models the residual around a pretrained surrogate's prediction, then is tuned by RL on trajectory-level rewards from multiple sampled rollouts.
tzEomMtqDX.evidence: Experiments across diverse surrogate architectures and PDE tasks; specific datasets and models are not named in the abstract.

lxLiDWpG89.one_liner: Identifies sparse MLP neurons that fire strongly when useful context is scarce, and links them to first-over-middle retrieval bias.
lxLiDWpG89.problem: Transformers apply the same blocks at every position although causal masking limits available context near sequence beginnings, and it is unclear how models process positions with little useful context.
lxLiDWpG89.method: The authors identify neuron sink, a sparse subset of MLP neurons with disproportionately frequent strong activations near sequence beginnings, which reappear at the start of a passage after an irrelevant prefix. They ablate sink neurons and, in a controlled model, transplant the sequence-initial sink-neuron state to middle positions.
lxLiDWpG89.key_idea: Sink neurons activate based on availability of useful context rather than absolute position; ablating them hurts early prediction and transplanting their initial state to middle positions reduces primacy bias.
lxLiDWpG89.evidence: Observed across diverse language models; ablation impairs prediction near sequence beginnings, and a state transplant in a controlled model reduces first-over-middle retrieval bias.

PHijX6QxNl.one_liner: Trains a robotic value model on timestamp-derived temporal distance to the goal, with shuffling and value-isolation attention against shortcuts.
PHijX6QxNl.problem: Existing reward-model supervision ties to task-internal anchors such as preferences or normalized progress, which do not transfer cleanly across embodiments and data sources.
PHijX6QxNl.method: TimeValue replaces those anchors with temporal distance, the directed cost-to-go from an observation to the language-specified goal, derived directly from timestamps, so it scales to over 7,000 hours and roughly 3M instruction-conditioned clips. It combines random temporal sampling, temporal-order shuffling, and value-isolation attention to suppress shortcuts.
PHijX6QxNl.key_idea: Supervise a value model with timestamp-derived temporal distance (cost-to-go to a language goal), using random sampling, order shuffling, and value-isolation attention to block shortcuts.
PHijX6QxNl.evidence: Trained on over 7,000 hours and roughly 3M clips and evaluated on RBM-EVAL-OOD, with zero-shot generalization to unseen tasks, embodiments, and viewpoints and use as a zero-shot reward model for downstream tasks.
PHijX6QxNl.claimed_gains: Average Kendall's tau_a of 0.704 on RBM-EVAL-OOD, versus 0.655 for the fully preference-supervised state of the art and 0.292 for a progress-only counterpart.

ws864CxRZs.one_liner: Optimizes a protective image perturbation plus a key embedding so unauthorized DiT editing fails but credentialed editing still works.
ws864CxRZs.problem: Existing perturbation-based protections disrupt reference use indiscriminately, so legitimate users also lose reference-consistent editing on protected images.
ws864CxRZs.method: Only the protected image and its key embedding are optimized, leaving the pretrained DiT editor unchanged. The visual perturbation disrupts unauthorized reference-conditioned editing, while the key embedding re-enables it for authorized users.
ws864CxRZs.key_idea: Pair a visual perturbation with a key embedding as an asymmetric control over the DiT's separate visual and text conditioning pathways, which jointly shape the same editing process.
ws864CxRZs.evidence: The abstract is cut off before any experiments; datasets, editors, and metrics are not visible.

9cqxQw3DMn.one_liner: Replaces sampled GRPO with exact optimization over all enumerable tool subsets using a precomputed reward table.
9cqxQw3DMn.problem: When the whole tool-subset space is enumerable, GRPO still estimates the action expectation from a few sampled rollouts, and as the policy concentrates, sampled rewards collide and group-normalized advantages vanish.
9cqxQw3DMn.method: FGPO (Full-Group Policy Optimization) scores every tool subset and optimizes the exact action expectation. It also precomputes the reward of each question-subset pair into an exhaustive table, removing reasoner calls from training.
9cqxQw3DMn.key_idea: Optimize the exact expectation over all tool subsets using a precomputed question-subset reward table, rather than estimating it from sampled rollouts.
9cqxQw3DMn.evidence: Five frozen reasoners and three genomic benchmarks (15 settings), including GenomeQA, compared against GRPO and (in a cut-off sentence) supervised baselines.
9cqxQw3DMn.claimed_gains: Outperforms GRPO in all 15 settings by 6.75 points on average and up to 14.20, at 3.5x lower end-to-end training cost, and on GenomeQA cuts invoked tools per question from 2.36 to 1.40.

6JfbrBLvFQ.one_liner: Proves what tying query-key or key-value projections in self-attention preserves and loses in expressivity.
6JfbrBLvFQ.problem: The effect of tying query, key, and value projections on the expressivity of self-attention is poorly understood.
6JfbrBLvFQ.method: The authors give a theoretical comparison of Q=K and K=V tying. Transformers with positional encodings stay universal approximators under full tying given sufficient depth, but individual heads face scheme-specific limits, which controlled synthetic experiments corroborate.
6JfbrBLvFQ.key_idea: Q=K makes attention logits Gram-structured, blocking cyclic-shift patterns, while K=V needs head dimension equal to the joint span of effective key and value subspaces.
6JfbrBLvFQ.evidence: Theorems on universality under full tying and head-level separations for Q=K and K=V, corroborated by controlled synthetic experiments.
6JfbrBLvFQ.claimed_gains: No empirical numbers stated; the K=V head dimension needed to reproduce an untied head can possibly be twice as large as in the untied case.

bymxVTMZg7.one_liner: Collects Android GUI screenshot-view hierarchy traces at scale with SoC clusters, VLM-assisted traversal, and human fallback.
bymxVTMZg7.problem: Training mobile GUI agents needs diverse interaction data across many apps, which is hard to collect, and prior mobile GUI datasets are limited in app diversity and scale.
bymxVTMZg7.method: MobileViews is built with a hardware-software pipeline combining native SoC clusters, VLM-assisted traversal, and selective human fallback, yielding over 1.2M unique screenshot-view hierarchy pairs with interaction traces from more than 30K Android apps. MobileViewsIDM adds over 81K inverse dynamics samples from 26K apps for training models to understand GUI transitions.
bymxVTMZg7.key_idea: Combine native SoC hardware clusters with VLM-guided app traversal and selective human fallback to collect traces from many apps.
bymxVTMZg7.evidence: Three VLMs trained on MobileViewsIDM are compared with training on prior mobile GUI datasets, and pipeline compatibility and traversal success are measured.
bymxVTMZg7.claimed_gains: Native app compatibility improves from 56% to 96% and traversal success rate from 16.7% to 89.6%; training on MobileViewsIDM generally outperforms prior datasets across the three VLMs, with no numbers given.

LVAnJjM4X1.one_liner: Stores reference anchor frames in a frozen autoregressive video model's KV cache, with drift-adaptive value amplification and anchor contrast guidance.
LVAnJjM4X1.problem: Autoregressive video models produce generic subjects from text rather than user-provided specific subjects, and existing customization needs per-subject optimization or bidirectional conditioning networks that do not suit causal streaming.
LVAnJjM4X1.method: Custom Forcing is training-free: it keeps reference-based anchor frames in the persistent KV cache of a frozen model. Drift-adaptive value amplification (DVA) scales reference influence with the degree of identity drift, and anchor contrast guidance (ACG) steers generation away from the generic class prior.
LVAnJjM4X1.key_idea: Scale reference influence in the KV cache by measured identity drift (DVA) and contrast against the generic class prior (ACG).
LVAnJjM4X1.evidence: Two-minute rollouts scored with DINO-I, plus comparisons with same- or larger-size subject-to-video models at short duration and with causal image-to-video and reference-to-video models over 30s.
LVAnJjM4X1.claimed_gains: Over two-minute rollouts, fixed anchors fall from 0.58 to 0.42 in DINO-I while Custom Forcing stays between 0.58 and 0.62, and over 30s it generates each frame 9.0-26.9x faster than causal image-to-video and reference-to-video models.

C64mPfypN7.one_liner: Uses routing replay to jointly plan sample and expert placement, balancing attention, expert compute, and All-to-All traffic in MoE RL.
C64mPfypN7.problem: Variable-length rollout samples and skewed expert routing cause GPU load imbalance across attention computation, expert computation, and routed All-to-All communication, and existing techniques address only subsets of these costs.
C64mPfypN7.method: J-MoE reuses the routing decisions recorded during rollout (routing replay), so each sample's expert demand is known before training. A two-stage solver with a unified cost model first assigns samples to microbatches and GPUs for each optimizer step, then jointly optimizes sample and expert placement per microbatch.
C64mPfypN7.key_idea: Routing replay reveals each sample's exact expert demand in advance, enabling a unified cost model and two-stage solver for joint sample-expert placement.
C64mPfypN7.evidence: A system for MoE RL post-training; the abstract is cut off before results, and the TL;DR reports the speedup.
C64mPfypN7.claimed_gains: Up to 1.8x speedup in MoE RL training (from the TL;DR).

2hkHTTSexE.one_liner: Turns implicit reward extrapolation into closed-form velocity regression for on-policy distillation, using a mildly degraded reference.
2hkHTTSexE.problem: RL post-training of flow-matching models gives high-variance gradients and cross-task interference, while conventional on-policy distillation only imitates the teacher.
2hkHTTSexE.method: DreOPD converts implicit reward extrapolation into closed-form velocity regression, giving extrapolative post-training with the stability of OPD. It uses a mildly degraded reference to strengthen the teacher-reference contrast and give a clearer extrapolation direction.
2hkHTTSexE.key_idea: Regress the student's velocity onto a closed-form extrapolation target built from the teacher and a mildly degraded reference.
2hkHTTSexE.evidence: Single-teacher and multi-teacher settings, compared with OPD and multi-task RL baselines; datasets and metrics are not named in the abstract.
2hkHTTSexE.claimed_gains: No numbers stated; reports higher average performance than OPD and multi-task RL baselines and surpassing specialized teachers on most metrics.
