bxbncwWzXX.one_liner: Shows low-confidence remasking, not arbitrary-order decoding, causes diversity loss in diffusion LLMs, and replaces it with top-probability position selection.
bxbncwWzXX.problem: Masked diffusion LMs support arbitrary-order generation, yet recent work argues this flexibility reduces diversity, which limits exploration in rollouts.
bxbncwWzXX.method: The authors show that low-confidence remasking (LCR) samples a token at every masked position but commits only the highest-probability one, exponentially suppressing lower-probability tokens as more positions compete. Top-probability position selection (TPP) instead picks the position whose most likely token has the highest probability and samples directly from that position's distribution; Entropy-Guided Initialization (EGI) then samples the first token (abstract cut off).
bxbncwWzXX.key_idea: Select the position whose most likely token has the highest probability, then sample from that position's distribution, instead of filtering sampled tokens by confidence.
bxbncwWzXX.evidence: Analysis of LCR suppression, with the same suppression observed in LLaDA, and Pass@k comparisons against left-to-right decoding.
bxbncwWzXX.claimed_gains: Replacing LCR with TPP restores diversity and yields Pass@k comparable to left-to-right decoding; no numbers are stated.

tKUm8meEUt.one_liner: Accepts physical-randomization range expansions only if the policy stays feasible and keeps prior performance, restoring policy state after failures.
tKUm8meEUt.problem: In on-policy RL, expanding physical randomization changes both the control problem and the trajectories driving learning, and retracting a failed expansion cannot undo learner updates that erode acquired behavior.
tKUm8meEUt.method: HORIZON is a recoverable curriculum that treats physical-domain expansion as a coupled update of the training distribution and learning state. It accepts an expansion only when the updated policy satisfies candidate-range feasibility and retains performance under previously accepted conditions; after failure it restores the accepted ranges and learning state while preserving the failed boundary for refinement.
tKUm8meEUt.key_idea: Couple range expansion with learner-state restoration: accept only verified expansions, and on failure roll back ranges and learning state but keep the failed boundary.
tKUm8meEUt.evidence: Quadruped locomotion under joint physical shifts compared with OpenAI ADR and GRAM, plus hardware transfer under payload changes, joint constraints, and leg extensions.
tKUm8meEUt.claimed_gains: 36.8% success under the strongest joint physical shift, compared with 19.8% for OpenAI ADR and 22.7% for GRAM.

1jS6kq4JQL.one_liner: Relaxes feature acquisition continuously so pathwise gradients flow through full acquisition trajectories, trained with straight-through rollouts.
1jS6kq4JQL.problem: Standard score-function policy gradients for active feature acquisition have high variance, and the goal is a non-myopic acquisition policy optimized end to end.
1jS6kq4JQL.method: A continuous relaxation of the acquisition process gives pathwise policy gradients through the full trajectory. A straight-through rollout follows discrete acquisitions in the forward pass while backpropagating through the soft relaxation, and an AFA-specific average-case variance bound motivates staged temperature sharpening.
1jS6kq4JQL.key_idea: Relax discrete feature acquisitions to a soft process and backpropagate through the whole trajectory with a straight-through rollout and staged temperature sharpening.
1jS6kq4JQL.evidence: Synthetic and real-world datasets compared against AFA baselines, plus a derived average-case variance upper bound for the gradient estimator.

mJr4tXbGvH.one_liner: Generates crystals by reversing a Markovian jump-diffusion from lowest-symmetry priors, transitioning between space groups.
mJr4tXbGvH.problem: Current generative models produce crystals only up to site symmetries and sample space groups from empirical distributions at inference, so they do not capture full crystallographic specifications.
mJr4tXbGvH.method: Inspired by spontaneous symmetry breaking, SbCD uses a Markovian jump-diffusion process to model symmetry-breaking dynamics, explicitly incorporating inter-space-group transitions into the generative process.
mJr4tXbGvH.key_idea: Model space-group transitions as jumps in a Markovian jump-diffusion that reverses from lowest-symmetry priors to full crystallographic specifications.
mJr4tXbGvH.evidence: De novo crystal generation experiments comparing against a symmetry-preserving counterpart, with thermodynamic stability reported on MPTS-52.

D4DEFRJ7ZQ.one_liner: Trains a dense audio-visual captioner with a bidirectional time-semantic alignment reward, plus a 50K dataset and a benchmark.
D4DEFRJ7ZQ.problem: Dense audio-visual captioning lacks a dataset with high temporal resolution, longer videos, and time-event alignment; existing RL methods rely on checklists; and no benchmark evaluates semantic correctness and temporal accuracy bidirectionally.
D4DEFRJ7ZQ.method: The authors build AVTime-50K, a 50K-scale dataset with temporally precise captions, train AVTime with a Bidirectional Temporal-Semantic Alignment (BiTSA) reward that imposes explicit bidirectional constraints between time and events, and release AVTime-Bench for bidirectional evaluation.
D4DEFRJ7ZQ.key_idea: The BiTSA reward constrains time-to-event and event-to-time alignment jointly during RL, rather than scoring captions against checklists.
D4DEFRJ7ZQ.evidence: The abstract describes the dataset, model, and benchmark but gives no experimental results, datasets, or baselines.

GWBPicZRkT.one_liner: Trains video LLMs for multi-interval temporal grounding with consensus-built labels and a temporal Wasserstein reward.
GWBPicZRkT.problem: Existing training for set-valued temporal grounding relies on brittle one-pass annotation for long videos, and RL rewards either fail to distinguish non-overlapping predictions or require fragile segment matching.
GWBPicZRkT.method: TimeLens2-93K builds multi-span supervision through caption-derived proposals, independent localization, cross-agent consensus, semantic verification, and boundary refinement. A temporal Wasserstein reward computes exact one-dimensional W1 between uniform distributions over merged interval supports, complemented by temporal IoU.
GWBPicZRkT.key_idea: Reward interval-set predictions with exact one-dimensional W1 distance between uniform distributions over merged interval supports, avoiding segment matching.
GWBPicZRkT.evidence: Seven benchmarks, with 2B, 4B, and 8B model variants compared against size-matched baselines and larger open-source models.
GWBPicZRkT.claimed_gains: TimeLens2-2B outperforms all size-matched baselines on every one of seven benchmarks, and the 4B and 8B variants achieve state-of-the-art performance, surpassing open-source models with up to 397B parameters.

Zh4k6rhTD7.one_liner: Separates rubric criteria discovery from search-based fact verification to train deep research agents with reinforcement learning.
Zh4k6rhTD7.problem: Rubric synthesis methods accept newly generated criteria without independent verification, inducing reward hacking toward verbosity, superficial reasoning, and ungrounded demands, and existing datasets have limited domain coverage.
Zh4k6rhTD7.method: RubricAtlas builds a four-level taxonomy with 234 leaf concepts for task synthesis, and Decoupled Rubric Discovery and Validation (DRDV) separates depth-oriented criteria discovery from search-augmented factual verification to filter ungrounded constraints. A Memo Context Manager keeps structured findings and evidence provenance, and a Group reward-Decoupled Normalization Policy Optimization handles policy optimization (abstract cut off).
Zh4k6rhTD7.key_idea: Verify each discovered rubric criterion with search-augmented fact checking in a separate stage before it is used as a reward.
Zh4k6rhTD7.evidence: The abstract is cut off before any experiments; datasets, baselines, and metrics are not visible.

fMLtNPrk34.one_liner: Re-perturbs one-step VSR student outputs to low noise levels and distills teacher denoising corrections, plus cross-frame relation alignment.
fMLtNPrk34.problem: One-step VSR models distilled with DMD keep frame-wise perceptual quality but show temporal artifacts such as flickering and texture drift, because cross-frame consistency is refined mostly at low noise levels that one-step distillation bypasses.
fMLtNPrk34.method: TRD-VSR re-perturbs student predictions to low-noise states and distills the teacher's local denoising corrections there. Relational Structure Alignment (RSA) additionally transfers cross-frame relational structure, and the framework is used only in training so inference stays single-step.
fMLtNPrk34.key_idea: Re-noise student outputs to low-noise states and match the teacher's local denoising corrections there, where temporal consistency is refined.
fMLtNPrk34.evidence: Three benchmarks, compared with existing one-step VSR methods on tLPIPS, tOF, tLP, CLIPIQA, and DOVER.
fMLtNPrk34.claimed_gains: Best tLPIPS across all datasets, best tOF and tLP on two datasets, and best CLIPIQA and DOVER across all datasets; no numeric values are stated.

ZKdBab2WX6.one_liner: Predicts each visual token's effect on correct-response likelihood, then prunes redundancy with a score-constrained determinantal point process.
ZKdBab2WX6.problem: Attention-based and feature-similarity-based visual token pruning use proxies that mismatch the objective of preserving the correct response.
ZKdBab2WX6.method: PerfPruner annotates a small training set with likelihood-based token importance, trains a lightweight predictor to estimate importance at test time, and applies a score-constrained determinantal point process (SDPP) to reduce redundancy among retained tokens.
ZKdBab2WX6.key_idea: Measure token importance as the likelihood change of the correct response, distill it into a lightweight predictor, and reduce redundancy with SDPP.
ZKdBab2WX6.evidence: 12 benchmarks across six tasks (safety, hallucination, general understanding, reasoning VQA, text-rich/OCR, chart/diagram understanding), varying pruning ratios and image resolutions.

Jjh60xpFVY.one_liner: Defines agent plasticity as held-out gain per unit learning cost and measures it across frontier models.
Jjh60xpFVY.problem: Agent evaluations mostly measure what agents can do, not how effectively they learn through experience.
Jjh60xpFVY.method: The authors study persistent self-improvement with frozen model weights, where agents build and refine tools, skills, memories, and strategies that future instances inherit, and define plasticity as the efficiency of improving future performance with more experience. They trace failures through the improvement loop on held-out in-distribution games and harder out-of-distribution games.
Jjh60xpFVY.key_idea: Quantify self-improvement as held-out performance gain per unit learning cost with weights frozen, and trace failures through the artifact build-and-reuse loop.
Jjh60xpFVY.evidence: Frontier models compared on held-out in-distribution and harder out-of-distribution games, with failure tracing through the improvement loop.

FpBiPA2CsW.one_liner: Coarsens graphs by greedily contracting nodes using Ollivier-Ricci curvature agreement, with a Kruskal-style algorithm maximizing a lower bound.
FpBiPA2CsW.problem: Existing coarsening methods use adjacency rules or Laplacian preservation without modeling metric-measure geometry, and Gromov-Wasserstein coarsening needs costly global distance and assignment computations.
FpBiPA2CsW.method: ORGC defines Ricci Geometric Coherence (RGC), which measures all-pairs curvature agreement among nodes contracted together, derives a contraction-forest lower bound for it, and maximizes the bound exactly with a Kruskal-style greedy algorithm. It also proves a boundary-preservation guarantee under a forest-rank separation condition.
FpBiPA2CsW.key_idea: Use Ollivier-Ricci curvature as an efficient geometric primitive for comparing Markov neighborhoods, and greedily maximize a contraction-forest lower bound on curvature coherence.
FpBiPA2CsW.evidence: Experiments on structural fidelity, graph classification, molecular regression, and runtime scaling, plus a boundary-preservation guarantee.

GtdDqnEsW7.one_liner: Benchmark of 1,000 videos evaluating video world models on physical faithfulness, geometric consistency, and interaction fidelity.
GtdDqnEsW7.problem: Existing benchmarks focus on visual quality, semantic alignment, or short-term coherence and say little about whether generated videos obey physical rules, keep 3D structure coherent, and sustain controllable long-horizon interactions.
GtdDqnEsW7.method: WorldOlympiad has a physical track (object segmentation and MLLM-as-judge on mechanics, thermal phenomena, and material properties), a geometry track (Gaussian-splatting reconstruction of generated videos scored for structural consistency, cross-view coherence, and camera-trajectory alignment), and an interaction track (action-prompt following and smooth transitions across consecutive chunks), over gaming, robotics, and real-world scenarios.
GtdDqnEsW7.key_idea: Decompose world-model evaluation into physical, geometry (via Gaussian-splatting reconstruction), and interaction tracks across gaming, robotics, and real-world scenes.
GtdDqnEsW7.evidence: Benchmark construction only; no model results are visible in the abstract.

cDud0Ztrwv.one_liner: Pretrains nGPT-style models with channel-shared residual coefficients, Muon, and norm constraints to reduce quantization outliers.
cDud0Ztrwv.problem: Low-bit PTQ fails when a few coordinates set the quantization range or high-gain directions amplify local errors, and a matched nGPT baseline concentrates residual-stream energy in one outlier channel, degrading 4-bit activation quantization.
cDud0Ztrwv.method: QuantRet builds on the normalized Transformer (nGPT), using channel-shared residual coefficients and training hidden matrices with Muon, while retracting activations to fixed-radius spheres and constraining hidden weight-matrix norms; its three variants differ in which norm is constrained.
cDud0Ztrwv.key_idea: Retract activations to spheres, constrain weight-matrix norms, and share residual coefficients across channels that share a quantization range, limiting outlier channel energy.
cDud0Ztrwv.evidence: Qwen3-like models under round-to-nearest quantization of weights, activations, and the KV cache, plus an analysis bounding perturbation injection through spherical residual mixing.

SsVGn88J0y.one_liner: Defines decision-alignment for uncertainty metrics and proposes prior-weighted utility metrics, a class of proper scoring rules.
SsVGn88J0y.problem: Common uncertainty metrics such as negative log-likelihood and expected calibration error do not necessarily reflect downstream decision utility.
SsVGn88J0y.method: The authors introduce decision-alignment, a criterion for which metrics faithfully rank models by decision-making performance, show that many widely used metrics are misaligned or encode implausible prior beliefs about the downstream task, and propose prior-weighted utility metrics as a special class of proper scoring rules.
SsVGn88J0y.key_idea: Check whether a metric ranks models as their realized decision utility does, and use prior-weighted utility metrics, proper scoring rules built to match that ranking.
SsVGn88J0y.evidence: Benchmark experiments and real-world case studies comparing the proposed metrics with conventional ones against realized decision utility.

7a59sIs39j.one_liner: Plug-in controller picks per-input context compression budgets from offline task feedback, calibrated to bound frequency of utility drops.
7a59sIs39j.problem: A fixed retention budget across inputs can discard needed evidence in some cases and keep unnecessary content in others, while evaluating task quality at several budgets per input would need repeated task-model calls.
7a59sIs39j.method: DiffContext is a task-aware budget controller for existing compressors with adjustable budgets. With the compressor and task model frozen, it uses offline task feedback to estimate harm and token cost across budgets, builds input-dependent policies, and uses independent calibration to select a deployment policy that limits the population frequency of utility drops (abstract cut off).
7a59sIs39j.key_idea: Estimate harm and token cost per budget from offline feedback to set input-dependent budgets, then calibrate independently to control the frequency of utility drops.
7a59sIs39j.evidence: The abstract is cut off before any experiments; datasets, compressors, and metrics are not visible.

LUrQEH43d5.one_liner: Distills a rubric-informed teacher into a rubric-free student on student rollouts for token-level personalization supervision.
LUrQEH43d5.problem: Rubric-guided personalization uses rubrics only coarsely, either to supervise aspect prediction or as a single response-level RL reward, leaving a gap between specifying what an answer should contain and teaching the model how to generate it.
LUrQEH43d5.method: GRASP pairs a rubric-free student with a rubric-informed teacher that also receives the user-specific rubrics, aligning their next-token distributions along on-policy trajectories generated by the student. Rubric-based Teacher Validation (RTV) is added because rubric-informed teachers can still give inadequate supervision (abstract cut off).
LUrQEH43d5.key_idea: Align a rubric-informed teacher's next-token distribution with a rubric-free student along on-policy rollouts, giving dense token-level rubric supervision.
LUrQEH43d5.evidence: The abstract is cut off before any experiments; datasets, baselines, and metrics are not visible.

DH20FhvpGM.one_liner: Edits recent street views into historical ones using satellite change evidence, trained with SFT then multi-reward Flow-GRPO.
DH20FhvpGM.problem: Historical street-view coverage is uneven, and generating plausible past appearances requires restoring changed structures while preserving persistent scene content.
DH20FhvpGM.method: The authors build VIGOR-his, a decade-spanning cross-view dataset of 43,653 location-level quadruplets across 11 cities on three continents, then train CrossTimeEdit from FLUX.2 [Klein] 4B with SFT followed by online RL using Flow-GRPO with GDPO over three criteria: Instruction Alignment, Background Preservation, and Quality and Physical Plausibility.
DH20FhvpGM.key_idea: Reformulate historical street-view generation as editing, constrained by recent street views and conditioned on temporal satellite differences, optimized with per-reward-normalized GDPO.
DH20FhvpGM.evidence: The VIGOR-his dataset; the three editing criteria serve as both RL rewards and evaluation metrics, and the results are cut off in the abstract.

cAyqQ6lwIW.one_liner: Quantization-aware distillation: a full-precision teacher steers failed student turns in a closed loop; corrections are then internalized.
cAyqQ6lwIW.problem: Low-bit quantized LLM agents overlook task requirements or environmental conditions and diverge from successful full-precision rollouts, and offline data or the student's own rollouts rarely supply correct responses in those failure contexts.
cAyqQ6lwIW.method: A full-precision teacher guides the student to revise failed responses and iteratively refines its guidance using feedback from student execution, yielding locally verified corrections. The unguided student is then trained to match the steered student's predictions at corrected turns and the full-precision teacher's elsewhere.
cAyqQ6lwIW.key_idea: Closed-loop teacher steering produces verified corrections at failed turns, which are distilled so the quantized student matches them without guidance at inference.
cAyqQ6lwIW.evidence: Five agentic benchmarks and three models under W4A16, with a tau2-Bench comparison against QeRL.
cAyqQ6lwIW.claimed_gains: Exceeds the strongest quantized baseline by 1.67-2.18 points in average score under W4A16 and stays within one point of BF16; on tau2-Bench it outperforms QeRL by 1.84 percentage points in success rate using 67% fewer training GPU hours.

QCzOM0Hnod.one_liner: Benchmark unifying DDI datasets, adding LLM-augmented datasets and multimodal drug representation, with standardized evaluation of baselines.
QCzOM0Hnod.problem: DDI prediction research relies on small datasets and single-modal drug representations, and evaluation scenarios, metrics, and baselines are inconsistent.
QCzOM0Hnod.method: OpenDDI unifies 6 widely used DDI datasets and 2 existing drug representations, adds 3 new large-scale LLM-augmented datasets and a new multimodal drug representation covering 5 modalities, and evaluates 20 baselines across 3 downstream tasks with standardized protocols for data quality, effectiveness, generalization, robustness, and efficiency.
QCzOM0Hnod.key_idea: Standardize data and evaluation protocols across DDI link-prediction methods, enriched with LLM-augmented data and multimodal drug representations.
QCzOM0Hnod.evidence: 20 SOTA baselines across 3 downstream tasks, evaluated for data quality, effectiveness, generalization, robustness, and efficiency.
QCzOM0Hnod.claimed_gains: Derives 11 insights for DDI prediction from the evaluation; no performance numbers are stated.

ae0Tjshnen.one_liner: Learns continuous latent actions from diverse videos with a shared orthogonal dictionary, conditioning world models via lightweight adapters.
ae0Tjshnen.problem: World models across domains need a unified control space, but action interfaces differ and annotations are scarce, and shared latent actions tend to entangle domain-specific visual cues with transferable transition structure.
ae0Tjshnen.method: OneLA learns continuous latent actions through a shared orthogonal dictionary and a common predictive objective, with no task-specific designs or cross-domain alignment losses in pretraining. Lightweight adapters map native control commands into the latent space, and the world model predicts context-dependent transitions from latent actions and the current visual state.
ae0Tjshnen.key_idea: Constrain latent actions to a shared orthogonal dictionary under one predictive objective so transitions share a cross-domain control space.
ae0Tjshnen.evidence: Action readout across domains, action cycle-transfer rotation error against the strongest evaluated baseline, and a joint-training comparison using HPSv3 on real-scene generation.
ae0Tjshnen.claimed_gains: Reduces action cycle-transfer rotation error by 24.8% over the strongest evaluated baseline and improves HPSv3 by 20.5% in a joint-training comparison for real-scene generation.

qxPLi2aZH7.one_liner: Persistent harness where foundation models revise executable scientific simulators using distributional discrepancy feedback against real signals.
qxPLi2aZH7.problem: Scientific simulator authoring has no unique implementation or exact test, so simulators must be judged against limited real observations.
qxPLi2aZH7.method: SimAuthor retains and revises executable simulators, separates scalar search scores from structured discrepancy feedback, and accumulates reusable implementation mechanisms.
qxPLi2aZH7.key_idea: Keep scalar search scores separate from structured discrepancy feedback while persisting simulators and reusable mechanisms across revisions.
qxPLi2aZH7.evidence: Six biomedical tasks (cardiac and respiratory audio, PPG, ECG) under a fixed 100-attempt budget against PUCT score search and textual-strategy optimization, plus unseen recordings, transfer to pretrained representations, and downstream ECG classification.
qxPLi2aZH7.claimed_gains: Under a fixed 100-attempt budget, outperforms PUCT score search on all six tasks and achieves the highest endpoint score on five of six.

IUi7QWlxPn.one_liner: Hierarchical planner generating variable-length latent subgoal routes and action prefixes via insertion-based flow matching, so plan length is an output.
IUi7QWlxPn.problem: Generative planners for offline goal-conditioned RL fix the planning horizon before generating content, though the right horizon depends on the route: too short forces infeasible transitions and too long adds redundant motion.
IUi7QWlxPn.method: A subgoal route planner generates a variable-length sequence of latent subgoals and an action-prefix controller generates a short variable-length action sequence toward the current subgoal, both combining insertion-based generation with flow matching to generate content and length jointly. Candidates are selected and steered by their generated length, without a separately trained value function.
IUi7QWlxPn.key_idea: Generate plan length jointly with plan content by insertion-based flow matching, using the partially generated plan to guide token insertion.
IUi7QWlxPn.evidence: Maze2D, Multi2D, OGBench navigate, and visual manipulation tasks, compared with other methods.
IUi7QWlxPn.claimed_gains: Highest average performance among the compared methods on the evaluated tasks; no numbers are stated.

xYpx0Tal4h.one_liner: Uses wavelet-energy profile of LM token scores to pick spans to rewrite, then selects replacements by rescored energy.
xYpx0Tal4h.problem: Making LLM text more human-like with minimal edits requires choosing which passages to revise and suitable replacements.
xYpx0Tal4h.method: A pretrained LM scores tokens from its next-token predictions, wavelet analysis turns the scores into an energy profile aligned with text positions, and short spans are selected for rewriting. A second LM generates candidates, each is inserted and rescored, and the one with the highest average energy over its span is kept, with no feedback from the target detector.
xYpx0Tal4h.key_idea: One shared wavelet-energy signal over token scores guides both which spans to rewrite and which candidate replacement to keep.
xYpx0Tal4h.evidence: A primary evaluation across fifteen domains against limited-edit baselines, with transfer to several additional detector families.
xYpx0Tal4h.claimed_gains: At thresholds calibrated to a 1% false-positive rate, an average of 80.8% of initially detected texts evade detection after rewriting, with greater detection reduction and less textual change than the compared limited-edit baselines.

1MYS2bXNlE.one_liner: Rebuilds a teacher one reward-gradient step ahead of the actor each iteration; its log ratio gives token advantages.
1MYS2bXNlE.problem: On-policy distillation with reward-trained experts commonly follows a train-then-distill workflow.
1MYS2bXNlE.method: OPGD rebuilds the teacher from the current actor at every iteration, one reward-gradient step ahead, so it inherits accumulated learning while adapting to fresh verified outcomes. The teacher-actor log ratio then supplies signed token advantages for OPD on the same rollouts.
1MYS2bXNlE.key_idea: Use the log ratio between a teacher one reward-gradient step ahead of the actor and the actor itself as signed token-level advantages.
1MYS2bXNlE.evidence: Four mathematical benchmarks on Qwen3-4B, with gains also on Qwen3-8B and OLMo 3 7B Instruct, separate coding-prompt training on three code-generation benchmarks, and a first-order analysis.
1MYS2bXNlE.claimed_gains: On Qwen3-4B, mean Pass@1 improves over GRPO by 9.2 percentage points across four mathematical benchmarks at a common 100-update budget, and gains persist on Qwen3-8B and OLMo 3 7B Instruct.

fWVkoV0NTZ.one_liner: Uses one synthesized rubric to filter supervised multimodal code data and then reward RL on visual-coding tasks.
fWVkoV0NTZ.problem: Open progress in multimodal code intelligence is held back by data quantity and quality, since no existing signal covers program correctness, good construction, and visual correctness once rendered.
fWVkoV0NTZ.method: PrismaForge is a hierarchical data pipeline centered on a synthesized rubric that decomposes these factors into checkable criteria; the rubric curates the supervised corpus (PrismaCoder-2M) and then drives reinforcement learning on visual-coding tasks.
fWVkoV0NTZ.key_idea: A single synthesized rubric of checkable criteria serves as both data gatekeeper and RL reward.
fWVkoV0NTZ.evidence: The abstract is cut off before results; the TL;DR says the models rival proprietary systems.

ljBEQztbhW.one_liner: Constrains a quasimetric critic's value gradients with finite-horizon reachability, estimating dynamical reachability and boundary geometry from offline data.
ljBEQztbhW.problem: Local constraints in quasimetric goal-conditioned RL should reflect the direction-dependent effects of control composition over a finite horizon together with environmental feasibility.
ljBEQztbhW.method: ReQRL constrains the critic's value gradients through finite-horizon reachability. Drawing on state-constrained optimal control, it decouples dynamical reachability from boundary geometry and estimates both from data.
ljBEQztbhW.key_idea: Bound the quasimetric critic's value gradients by finite-horizon reachability, with reachability and boundary geometry estimated separately from data.
ljBEQztbhW.evidence: Evaluated on OGBench against quasimetric approaches and other offline GCRL methods.
ljBEQztbhW.claimed_gains: Outperforms or rivals existing quasimetric approaches and other offline GCRL methods on OGBench; no numbers are stated.

I9sF2v1sOi.one_liner: Training-free sub-one-bit KV cache compression: residual vector quantization forms a persistent base, extra bits refine it within budget.
I9sF2v1sOi.problem: The growing KV cache of autoregressive video generation is impractical to keep at high precision under limited GPU memory, and discarding past states or lowering their precision compromises consistency in appearance, structure, and motion.
I9sF2v1sOi.method: SuBitKV builds a low-memory persistent base with residual vector quantization, which jointly represents each key or value vector with a small set of compact indices, then allocates additional bits across the cache within the memory budget, shrinking these extra bits as the cache grows.
I9sF2v1sOi.key_idea: Represent each key/value vector with residual vector quantization indices as a persistent base, and spend remaining budget on extra bits that shrink as the cache grows.
I9sF2v1sOi.evidence: Three video-generation and world-model backbones, with Wan2.2 as the detailed example, scored on VBench.
I9sF2v1sOi.claimed_gains: On Wan2.2, 21.42x compression with near-BF16 VBench scores, and 30.09x under tighter memory budgets.

6tfl7P150b.one_liner: Predicts an object-space visibility field from a partial point cloud and generated mesh, then aligns observation to visible mesh parts.
6tfl7P150b.problem: Scene generation either produces objects directly in scene coordinates, compromising canonical-space priors, or regresses poses from complete generated shapes, a poorly conditioned problem sensitive to scale ambiguity and partial observations.
6tfl7P150b.method: ScenePlacer reformulates alignment as conditional visibility-field learning on a pretrained 3D shape VAE backbone conditioned on a separately encoded partial observation, then estimates the rigid transformation by aligning the observation to visible mesh parts. It uses visibility-aware, radius-constrained supervision on training pairs synthesized from object-level meshes and rendered views, so no scene-level pose annotations are needed.
6tfl7P150b.key_idea: Recast pose estimation as predicting which parts of the generated mesh are visible in the partial observation, then align the observation to those parts.
6tfl7P150b.evidence: Comparisons on 3D-FUTURE against placement and pose-refinement baselines; the rest of the abstract is cut off.

Arptw2Lc8Q.one_liner: Continuous-latent diffusion language model: frozen query-based autoencoder latents modeled by a block-causal diffusion transformer with blockwise flow matching.
Arptw2Lc8Q.problem: Existing continuous language models inherit embedding spaces not designed for both generation and decoding, or compress latents to ease diffusion, possibly sacrificing token-level fidelity.
Arptw2Lc8Q.method: A Query-based Encoder-Decoder organizes text into a prefix-aligned latent sequence; the autoencoder is then frozen and a Block-causal Diffusion Transformer models the full-width latents with blockwise flow matching. The noisy-input pathway goes through a low-rank bottleneck while the clean-latent target stays full, noise levels are calibrated to latent width, and self-trajectory consistency bridges training and iterative-denoising inference.
Arptw2Lc8Q.key_idea: Keep high-capacity decodable text latents and ease diffusion by restricting only the noisy-input pathway to a low-rank bottleneck.
Arptw2Lc8Q.evidence: Evaluated with Gen-PPL and MAUVE; the benchmarks and baselines are cut off in the abstract.
Arptw2Lc8Q.claimed_gains: Reports the best Gen-PPL and MAUVE, but the abstract is cut off before values or benchmarks.

rpXERv433g.one_liner: Benchmark testing Video-LLMs on open-set video anomaly understanding with controlled known-unknown category splits and an unknown-anomaly rejection option.
rpXERv433g.problem: Video anomaly understanding systems may meet events outside a predefined category set and then pick an inappropriate available label.
rpXERv433g.method: OpenVA-Bench integrates 1,330 videos from three datasets with explicit Known-Unknown category splits (Normal in the Known set, Unknown Anomaly as a rejection option) and examines predictions, self-reported confidence, and explanations under controlled candidate-category exclusions.
rpXERv433g.key_idea: Exclude categories from the candidate list so models must reject unknown anomalies, and inspect confidence and explanations alongside predictions.
rpXERv433g.evidence: 25 Video-LLMs evaluated on 1,330 videos from three datasets.
rpXERv433g.claimed_gains: No performance numbers stated; findings are qualitative, e.g. stronger known-class recognition does not consistently coincide with reliable unknown rejection.

vVjAliqWmG.one_liner: Derives exact worst-case uncertainty about alternatives' quality once a robustly epsilon-optimal direction is selected from linear measurements.
vVjAliqWmG.problem: It is unclear how much uncertainty about the other candidates can remain after a choice is already justified, since choosing a good candidate need not require estimating every candidate well.
vVjAliqWmG.method: The authors study unit directions whose quality is the squared positive part of their cosine similarity with an unknown vector observed through exact linear measurements. They derive the exact worst-case uncertainty diameter of an alternative's quality given the selected quality theta, a location-sensitive bound on simultaneous intervals, and a lower bound on additional queries for randomized adaptive continuation.
vVjAliqWmG.key_idea: Given selected quality theta, the worst-case diameter of an alternative's quality is theta+epsilon below theta=epsilon/(1+2*epsilon) and 2*sqrt(epsilon(1+epsilon)theta(1-theta)) above it.
vVjAliqWmG.evidence: Theoretical derivations in which matching histories attain both branches of the bound; no empirical results are mentioned.
vVjAliqWmG.claimed_gains: For 0 < epsilon <= 1/2 the diameter is theta+epsilon below theta=epsilon/(1+2*epsilon) and 2*sqrt(epsilon(1+epsilon)theta(1-theta)) above it, and for 0 < epsilon <= 1/10 randomized adaptive continuation can require Omega(min{m, epsilon/eta^2}) additional queries.

RgyT1ytzsA.one_liner: Gradient-based test-time optimization of intermediate representations in a frozen VAR transformer using differentiable cross-attention constraints.
RgyT1ytzsA.problem: Visual autoregressive text-to-image models fail at attribute binding and spatial relations, and existing test-time methods search sampled trajectories or apply generic logit guidance without optimizing compositional constraints.
RgyT1ytzsA.method: Built on Infinity, VISTA optimizes intermediate representations through the frozen transformer with no parameter updates or training, and stabilizes the optimization across scales. It exposes an interface where any differentiable cross-attention constraint can be plugged in.
RgyT1ytzsA.key_idea: Backpropagate a differentiable cross-attention compositional constraint into intermediate representations of a frozen next-scale VAR transformer at test time.
RgyT1ytzsA.evidence: Two benchmarks and two model scales (2B and 8B backbones), plus a human evaluation and ImageReward scoring.
RgyT1ytzsA.claimed_gains: Raises the mean by nearly 20% on a 2B backbone and almost 6% on an 8B backbone, wins 83% of decisive compositionality comparisons in human evaluation, and ImageReward scores its outputs 20% higher.

hreW5dFUtw.one_liner: Multi-teacher distillation into an egocentric RGB encoder using learned proxies that translate nine heterogeneous teachers into one egocentric space.
hreW5dFUtw.problem: Egocentric RGB video gives a limited view of human actions, and richer privileged signals (other modalities, exocentric views, foundation models) are unavailable or impractical at inference.
hreW5dFUtw.method: PROXYDIST learns representation-specific proxies that translate nine heterogeneous teachers' knowledge into a homogeneous egocentric space, merges the proxies through a learned convex initialization, then applies Selective Proxy Distillation (SPD) to distill from the most reliable proxies for each training sample.
hreW5dFUtw.key_idea: Distill through per-teacher proxies mapped into the egocentric feature space instead of from incompatible teacher spaces directly, then selectively distill from the most reliable proxies per sample.
hreW5dFUtw.evidence: Action recognition, video retrieval, and action segmentation on three ego-exo benchmarks, compared against direct multi-teacher distillation.

GlbZrgNGVP.one_liner: Causal tracing with the AudioEvidence testbed maps how audio evidence enters language computation across nine LALMs.
GlbZrgNGVP.problem: It is unclear how large audio language models integrate task-relevant auditory evidence into language computation.
GlbZrgNGVP.method: They build AudioEvidence, a testbed with temporal evidence annotations, matched non-evidence controls, and counterfactual sound replacements, and apply causal interventions at the backbone input, across layers, and on attention heads in nine LALMs.
GlbZrgNGVP.key_idea: Intervene on audio-evidence states and attention access across layers and heads, using counterfactual sound replacements, to locate where evidence causally enters text computation.
GlbZrgNGVP.evidence: Causal interventions on nine LALMs with the AudioEvidence testbed; eight models share a depth-wise organization, and amplifying selected heads in MiMo-Audio is tested on audio hallucination detection and speech recognition.

vlSKh8xmjM.one_liner: Flow-based posterior sampling via Split Gibbs Sampling with annealed coupling, with timestep correction and one-step flow warm-up for inverse imaging.
vlSKh8xmjM.problem: Existing flow-based inverse solvers make simplifying approximations in posterior sampling or assume linear forward models, while principled diffusion-based methods are computationally expensive.
vlSKh8xmjM.method: FlowSGS runs Split Gibbs Sampling with annealed coupling using a flow prior, with flow-specific interventions to prior sampling and annealing grounded in the Stochastic Interpolants framework. It adds a timestep correction and a warm-up accelerated by one-step flow models.
vlSKh8xmjM.key_idea: Replace the prior-sampling step of Split Gibbs Sampling with Stochastic Interpolants-grounded flow sampling, using a timestep correction and one-step flow models to warm up the chain.
vlSKh8xmjM.evidence: A range of imaging problems including the nonlinear Fourier phase retrieval problem; specific datasets and baselines are not stated.

mi7dXjKm6m.one_liner: Few-step generation where a shared generator iteratively refines its prediction in data space, removing flow timestep discretization.
mi7dXjKm6m.problem: Existing few-step methods iterate along the probability flow and need a fixed, manually chosen timestep discretization that is expensive to tune and may not suit samples or locations with different refinement difficulty.
mi7dXjKm6m.method: Starting from noise, a shared generator repeatedly refines its prediction directly in data space, with each iteration trained to produce the best sample its capacity permits. The formulation plugs into distribution matching distillation (DMD) with minimal changes.
mi7dXjKm6m.key_idea: Iterate the generator's own data-space prediction instead of integrating the probability flow, training each iteration to give the best sample its capacity permits.
mi7dXjKm6m.evidence: Class-conditional ImageNet 256x256, compared with standard discretization baselines and schedule-search variants under matched DMD training settings.

Z1BrwFVJBd.one_liner: Binary latents learned by injecting symmetric noise after a bounded activation such as tanh, without a straight-through estimator.
Z1BrwFVJBd.problem: STE-based discrete representation learning such as VQ-VAE uses surrogate gradients, creating a forward/backward mismatch during encoder optimization.
Z1BrwFVJBd.method: MERVar-AE injects symmetric noise into the output of a bounded activation (e.g., tanh), which pushes outputs toward the boundaries and yields binary latents. Gradients propagate through the same continuous latent used in the forward pass.
Z1BrwFVJBd.key_idea: Noise injection before a deterministic decoder reduces overlap among random variables and makes them mutually exclusive, so a bounded activation plus noise saturates to binary values.
Z1BrwFVJBd.evidence: Experiments on nine standard datasets against state-of-the-art discrete representation learning methods, plus controlled experiments on surrogate-gradient mismatch.

sLG5Quwcrk.one_liner: Large multimodal 3D assembly dataset plus a VLM that autoregressively predicts 6-DoF trajectories as discrete pose tokens.
sLG5Quwcrk.problem: Existing benchmarks cover either 6-DoF pose reasoning or trajectory prediction in specialized regimes, leaving general process-level assembly learning across domains and initial configurations open.
sLG5Quwcrk.method: AssemblyVerse has 10,809 assemblies across five domains and 192,412 steps, each aligned with instruction diagrams, text, assembly states, and verified collision-free trajectories. AssemblyMind grounds each next step with an auxiliary order-grounding head and generates 6-DoF trajectories as reordered discrete pose tokens, trained with staging-randomized SFT and GV-GRPO.
sLG5Quwcrk.key_idea: Predict part order with an auxiliary grounding head, emit trajectories as discrete pose tokens, and optimize geometric validity directly with GV-GRPO.
sLG5Quwcrk.evidence: Extensive experiments on AssemblyVerse are mentioned, but the visible abstract does not give datasets or baselines beyond the dataset itself.

qQlbYBKmPW.one_liner: Graph neural ODE whose vector field averages graph-walk propagators under a state-conditioned distribution over walk lengths.
qQlbYBKmPW.problem: Existing graph ODEs use a predetermined hop structure within each vector-field evaluation, so propagation mass across spatial orders cannot adapt to the evolving state.
qQlbYBKmPW.method: PIANO's spatial operator is an expected finite-step graph-walk propagator under a state-conditioned distribution over walk lengths, with a lightweight topology-aware gate for node-wise modulation. It uses sparse graph operations whose cost scales linearly with maximum propagation order, edge count, and feature dimension.
qQlbYBKmPW.key_idea: Learn a state-dependent distribution over walk lengths and use the resulting expected multi-hop propagator as the ODE's spatial operator.
qQlbYBKmPW.evidence: Proofs of non-expansiveness, well-posedness of the nonlinear flow, and a finite-hop approximation radius for a frozen linear surrogate; controlled experiments; ocean and severe-weather forecasting.

RC3BjfXL7T.one_liner: Elastic transformer with dense-core-plus-shells hidden dimensions and a muP extension so all nested sub-networks train and transfer hyperparameters together.
RC3BjfXL7T.problem: Elastic supernet training has variable per-step workloads that hinder distributed scaling, limited hyperparameter transfer across model sizes, and no guarantee that all sub-networks are maximally updated at once.
RC3BjfXL7T.method: ShellElastic organizes hidden dimensions into a dense core and successive shells so every hidden matrix is block lower triangular, and one full-width forward pass contains every sub-network's hidden states as prefixes. mu-Elastic extends muP with scaling rules that keep all sub-networks maximally updated simultaneously.
RC3BjfXL7T.key_idea: Block lower-triangular hidden matrices make each sub-network a prefix of one full-width forward pass, and muP-style scaling rules keep all prefixes maximally updated.
RC3BjfXL7T.evidence: Hyperparameter sweeps from a small non-elastic proxy to elastic families and larger supernets, plus comparison with MatFormer and fully elastic baselines; results are truncated in the abstract.

61t0BCKEvo.one_liner: Prunes MoE experts by learning per-expert router biases with a routing-diversity regularizer, then approximating pruned experts with affine transforms.
61t0BCKEvo.problem: Structured expert pruning in MoE models relies on ranking criteria poorly aligned with performance or on costly subset search, and ignores routing-behavior redundancy among retained experts.
61t0BCKEvo.method: MoRA learns a router bias per expert by minimizing language-modeling loss plus a routing-diversity regularizer; the biases sharpen routing distributions to identify critical experts and favor experts with diverse routing preferences. After pruning, the remaining experts approximate pruned experts' outputs via affine transformation.
61t0BCKEvo.key_idea: Router biases trained with language-modeling loss and a routing-diversity term rank experts for pruning, and affine maps over remaining experts approximate the removed ones.
61t0BCKEvo.evidence: An evaluation is mentioned but the abstract is truncated before models or datasets are named.

I0NjnTCuu8.one_liner: Learns log-likelihood ratios up to positive scale and selects checkpoints by Normalized Integrated Tradeoff Area (NITA).
I0NjnTCuu8.problem: Conventional validation criteria can favor checkpoints whose estimated LLR trajectories poorly match the true LLR shape, and test results alone cannot determine exact-scale LLR error because rescaling the LLR and thresholds together leaves decisions unchanged.
I0NjnTCuu8.method: They take the positive-projectivized LLR (P+LLR), the true LLR up to positive rescaling, as the estimand, define the validation metric NITA, and prove it is ordered with oracle P+LLR estimation error in a high-threshold detection task.
I0NjnTCuu8.key_idea: Estimate the LLR only up to positive scale, since rescaled thresholds give identical stopping decisions, and validate with an operating-curve area (NITA) ordered with P+LLR error.
I0NjnTCuu8.evidence: Proofs of NITA's ordering with oracle error under i.i.d. streams with independent noise, a finite-sample checkpoint-selection guarantee for empirical NITA, an extension to non-i.i.d., multiclass, and classification settings, and experiments on 12 diverse datasets.

AoRAueuPjw.one_liner: Uses MoE routing statistics from a frozen multimodal LLM as an anomaly cue to recalibrate semantic channels.
AoRAueuPjw.problem: Intermediate-layer features of multimodal LLMs are strong for video anomaly detection, yet the origin of their discriminative power is unclear.
AoRAueuPjw.method: With a frozen sparse-MoE backbone and no extra training, anomaly evidence is found concentrated in a small set of recurring, type-specialized experts forming a dynamic routing subnetwork. RoMod uses a Routing-Modulated Fusion module (RoMF) to recalibrate hidden semantic channels with routing signals, without letting the routing branch predict alone, and a Routing-aware Temporal Network (RoTN) to model anomaly evolution from onset to persistence.
AoRAueuPjw.key_idea: Treat expert routing statistics of a frozen MoE as an internal anomaly cue that modulates semantic hidden channels without bypassing them.
AoRAueuPjw.evidence: Analysis of a frozen sparse-MoE multimodal model showing anomaly evidence concentrated in few experts, and RoMod trained with only 5% weakly labeled videos (the abstract is truncated before the results).

7ah1goQmsX.one_liner: Self-distills a teacher grounded in similar users' optimal-transport-matched trajectories to give token-level credit in LLM sequential recommendation.
7ah1goQmsX.problem: LLM-based sequential recommenders post-trained with GRPO share one sequence-level reward across all tokens (credit-blind) and derive each training signal from a single user, ignoring patterns shared across similar users (collaborative-blind).
7ah1goQmsX.method: On-policy self-distillation lets a privileged teacher re-evaluate the student's on-policy response, and the token-level confidence difference reshapes the shared sequence-level advantage into token-specific credit. The teacher is grounded in similar users' behavior using temporally aware optimal transport that compares interaction trajectories by item similarity and temporal structure, followed by a diversity-aware step (abstract truncated).
7ah1goQmsX.key_idea: Use the token-level confidence gap between a retrieval-privileged teacher and the student to reshape sequence-level GRPO advantage, retrieving teacher evidence with temporally aware optimal transport.
7ah1goQmsX.evidence: Experiments are not described in the visible abstract, which is truncated before the results.

GYZUysAiKG.one_liner: Theory of weight averaging in LLM pretraining as a progress-versus-robustness trade-off, with a family of averaging kernels guiding post-training quantization.
GYZUysAiKG.problem: Weight averaging during pretraining can improve post-training quantization over learning-rate decay, but its mechanism is poorly explained, causing inconsistent and fragile gains.
GYZUysAiKG.method: The paper formulates weight averaging as a trade-off between retaining training progress and robustness under perturbation, derives a continuous family of averaging kernels that unifies conventional strategies on the Pareto frontier, and develops a theoretical framework for averaging under PTQ.
GYZUysAiKG.key_idea: Averaging kernels lie on a Pareto frontier between retained training progress and robustness to perturbation, and coarser quantization is more perturbation-sensitive.
GYZUysAiKG.evidence: Theoretical derivation of the kernel family and the PTQ framework, with experiments said to validate the predicted behavior and the proposed averaging strategy (details not given in the abstract).

pQkYUmK8lI.one_liner: Trains branching rules on proof cost from subtree rollouts with a known cutoff instead of imitating strong branching.
pQkYUmK8lI.problem: Learned branching rules imitate strong branching, whose score reflects only one-step LP bound improvement and ignores how the resulting subtrees are solved.
pQkYUmK8lI.method: On solved training instances, the known optimum sets the objective cutoff, and each candidate branch is followed by a fixed continuation rule until its subtree completes or a node budget is reached. Completed rollouts give exact proof costs and interrupted ones give certified lower bounds, defining hard, soft, and set-valued training targets.
pQkYUmK8lI.key_idea: Label branching candidates by rollout proof cost under the known-optimum cutoff, using lower bounds for interrupted rollouts, rather than by one-step LP bound gains.
pQkYUmK8lI.evidence: Three MILP families (multidimensional knapsack, combinatorial auctions, set cover) against matched behavior cloning and a compute-matched Branch Ranking collector, with information-source controls, a transfer test to a harder auction cohort, and a performance-difference identity for subtree-local proof trees.
pQkYUmK8lI.claimed_gains: Hindsight targets reduce held-out tree size relative to matched behavior cloning by up to 45% across three MILP families.

hBbWx5gK15.one_liner: Meta-trains sequential neural networks to jointly learn exploration, stopping, and recommendation for pure exploration over continuous recommendation spaces.
hBbWx5gK15.problem: Existing active sequential testing methods are mostly problem-specific, and learned approaches are limited to finite recommendation spaces.
hBbWx5gK15.method: They formulate Bayesian fixed-confidence pure exploration, characterize the Bellman structure of an ideal learner, and introduce C-ICPE. C-ICPE meta-trains sequential architectures over a task prior and, at inference, gathers evidence and returns a recommendation without parameter updates.
hBbWx5gK15.key_idea: Meta-train a sequential network over a task prior, guided by the Bellman structure of the ideal Bayesian learner, to output exploration, stopping, and recommendation in context.
hBbWx5gK15.evidence: Experiments on localization, identification, and value estimation problems; no datasets or baselines are named in the abstract.

seepJ1Y01P.one_liner: Feed-forward human-scene 4D reconstruction aligning human and scene priors via bidirectional anchoring and multi-view fusion.
seepJ1Y01P.problem: Independently trained human and scene priors misalign in scale and depth: the scene prior gives consistent depth but approximate scale, while the human prior gives fixed body scale but less reliable depth.
seepJ1Y01P.method: HARMONI reconstructs cameras, scene and identified humans from monocular or multi-view video without test-time optimization. Bidirectional anchoring lets scene depth guide human placement while human keypoints calibrate scene scale, and a multi-view fusion module merges per-view estimates while down-weighting unreliable views and look-alike individuals.
seepJ1Y01P.key_idea: Bidirectional anchoring: scene depth positions the humans, and human keypoints calibrate the scene scale to the body.
seepJ1Y01P.evidence: Comparisons against previous human-scene methods on global motion and multi-view pose estimation, and a runtime comparison with optimization-based approaches.
seepJ1Y01P.claimed_gains: Outperforms previous human-scene methods in global motion and multi-view pose estimation by up to 28% and 64%, while running 28x faster than optimization-based approaches.

ZzcmQVN3BX.one_liner: Proves a shallow transformer trained by gradient flow hallucinates fine-grained labels on hierarchical classification when nuance tokens are rare.
ZzcmQVN3BX.problem: The paper studies one form of hallucination, where a model puts high probability on the correct coarse class but near-chance probability on the correct fine-grained label.
ZzcmQVN3BX.method: In a hierarchical sequence classification problem, a common signal token encodes a coarse label and a rarer nuance token encodes a fine label. The paper proves the behavior of a shallow transformer under gradient flow when nuance tokens are sufficiently rare and token noise is small.
ZzcmQVN3BX.key_idea: Attention weights concentrate on the common signal tokens and suppress learning from the rare nuance token, creating a long training plateau in which the model hallucinates.
ZzcmQVN3BX.evidence: Gradient-flow theorems for a shallow transformer, plus experiments on an LLM-generated synthetic BirdText dataset showing coarse-to-fine learning.

XwweKmTLqV.one_liner: FastCI cuts GPU-heavy CI for LLM training frameworks via runtime-evidence test selection, pruning, risk-based prioritization, and workload reduction.
XwweKmTLqV.problem: CI for LLM training frameworks relies on GPU-intensive tests involving full model training or evaluation, which makes CI itself a bottleneck for fast-paced development.
XwweKmTLqV.method: FastCI uses runtime evidence to select affected tests and prune tests that execute changed code in equivalent contexts, prioritizes high-risk tests to expose failures earlier, and optimizes test workloads along dimensions outside each test's intended validation scope.
XwweKmTLqV.key_idea: Use runtime execution evidence to select affected tests and prune tests that exercise changed code in equivalent contexts, then reorder by risk and trim out-of-scope workload dimensions.
XwweKmTLqV.evidence: Evaluated on the CI workload of the authors' own LLM training framework against its currently deployed CI pipelines, plus production deployment.
XwweKmTLqV.claimed_gains: Reduces CI latency by 77.5% and GPU usage by 63.9% while improving modified-code coverage retention by 3.2%; in production it cut average CI latency by about 58.4% and saved 724,000 GPU-hours over 11 weeks.

LADMspX1Cd.one_liner: Trains a LoRA Writer to compile position-independent document KV caches via behavioral distillation, leaving the pretrained Reader decoder unchanged.
LADMspX1Cd.problem: Prefix caching cannot exploit document reuse under changing instructions, histories, and orders, while position-independent caching is unreliable because independently compiled KV states lack the context in which they will be consumed.
LADMspX1Cd.method: SemPIC trains a LoRA-enabled Writer to compile native per-layer document KVs through behavioral distillation while keeping the pretrained decoder unchanged as the Reader, confining adaptation to offline cache construction. It also adds KV Gradient Checkpointing, which reduces peak training memory without severing gradients through cached KVs.
LADMspX1Cd.key_idea: Adapt the document-side KV compiler, not the decoder, by behavioral distillation, so caches keep the standard KV interface and cache-hit decoding path.
LADMspX1Cd.evidence: Three models and four tasks compared with KV Packet and Full Recompute, plus diagnostics of attention deviation near reusable-block boundaries.
LADMspX1Cd.claimed_gains: Raises mean micro-F1 over KV Packet from 0.55 to 0.60, approaching Full Recompute at 0.62.

FbLFacZ5KP.one_liner: Adapts both class representation and query-class comparison in cross-domain few-shot learning using class-specific characteristic-function frequencies.
FbLFacZ5KP.problem: Metric-based cross-domain few-shot methods adapt class prototypes from target support examples but score all queries with one shared Euclidean or cosine metric.
FbLFacZ5KP.method: A plug-and-play module in which a KL-regularized stochastic generator conditions on a class's support set to produce class-specific frequency arguments for an empirical characteristic function; a query is tentatively added to each candidate support set and the change in the characteristic-function representation gives the membership score.
FbLFacZ5KP.key_idea: Score query membership by how much adding the query shifts a class's empirical characteristic function, with class-specific frequencies generated from the support set.
FbLFacZ5KP.evidence: not stated in the visible abstract, which is cut off before the experiments.

yjvjLBboWn.one_liner: Jointly learns weights with low-rank and structured-sparse components during pretraining, with CPU/GPU kernels exploiting the structure.
yjvjLBboWn.problem: Sparse-plus-low-rank compression gives elastic memory budgets, but indexing overhead and irregular memory access in unstructured sparse components can cancel the speedup from fewer parameters.
yjvjLBboWn.method: S-SALAAD jointly learns model weights and their low-rank and structured sparse components during training, supports a family of hardware-compatible sparsity patterns, and couples this with budget-aware compression. Dedicated CPU and GPU kernels exploit the learned structure.
yjvjLBboWn.key_idea: Impose hardware-compatible structured sparsity on the sparse component of a sparse-plus-low-rank decomposition during training, so one checkpoint compresses to several memory budgets with regular memory access.
yjvjLBboWn.evidence: Experiments on Llama2 and Qwen3 models covering pretraining and further settings that are cut off in the abstract text provided.

6XyVfTkAQ9.one_liner: Distribution-matching distillation where an extended-horizon bidirectional teacher supervises long student self-rollouts of autoregressive video models.
6XyVfTkAQ9.problem: Autoregressive video diffusion models drift when rolled out far beyond their training window (quality drops, motion becomes inconsistent, object identity collapses) because short-horizon distillation leaves later rollout states without direct supervision.
6XyVfTkAQ9.method: LongForcing keeps the short-horizon teacher-forcing and causal ODE-distillation stages and replaces the real-score teacher in the final distribution-matching stage with an extended-horizon bidirectional teacher. That teacher supervises extended student self-rollouts without changing the student architecture or inference cost.
6XyVfTkAQ9.key_idea: Scale the distribution-matching teacher to long on-policy student self-rollouts so delayed failures receive direct supervision (temporal manifold matching).
6XyVfTkAQ9.evidence: Evaluated on text-to-video generation and interactive action-conditioned world models, with VBench Quality reported (the score is cut off in the abstract text provided).
6XyVfTkAQ9.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract text provided cuts off at 'achieving a VBench Quality').

6AfNycPzQY.one_liner: Per-quantile queries attend over history patches to build quantile-specific contexts; a shared decoder predicts all quantiles in one pass.
6AfNycPzQY.problem: Direct probabilistic forecasters share one historical context across all quantiles, though different quantiles may benefit from different parts of the history.
6AfNycPzQY.method: QUEST splits the history into patches and encodes them into shared local representations. For each target quantile, a query computes patch weights conditioned on the history and the probability level, and a shared decoder combines each resulting context with its query to predict that quantile over the horizon.
6AfNycPzQY.key_idea: Condition attention weights over history patches on the target quantile level, so each quantile gets its own selected historical context.
6AfNycPzQY.evidence: Experiments on eight (datasets, as far as the abstract text provided shows; the rest is cut off).

65VC2PWo3C.one_liner: APUN-Bench benchmarks large audio-language models on pun recognition, pun word location, and pun meaning inference in speech.
65VC2PWo3C.problem: Datasets and systematic resources for audio puns are scarce, leaving audio pun understanding by large audio-language models underexplored.
65VC2PWo3C.method: Builds a benchmark of 4,447 audio samples annotated across three stages (pun recognition, pun word location, pun meaning inference) and evaluates 10 LALMs. Motivated by positional biases in localization and error patterns in meaning inference, it proposes a prompt-based strategy and a fine-tuning framework.
65VC2PWo3C.key_idea: Three-stage annotation of audio puns (recognition, word location, meaning inference), with prompting and fine-tuning fixes targeted at observed positional bias and error patterns.
65VC2PWo3C.evidence: Systematic evaluation of 10 large audio-language models on the 4,447-sample benchmark, plus analysis of positional biases and error patterns.
65VC2PWo3C.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract reports substantial performance gaps across 10 LALMs but no numeric gains for the proposed strategy.

RkBg2Ytoer.one_liner: Mechanistic analysis of how RoPE versus NoPE positional encoding choices shift in-context retrieval between positional and semantic mechanisms.
RkBg2Ytoer.problem: It is unclear how varying attention span and positional encoding across layers (for example RoPE with sliding-window attention and NoPE with global attention) shapes in-context retrieval.
RkBg2Ytoer.method: Traces the internal retrieval mechanisms of 22 open-weight models across eight families, runs a controlled pre-training ablation that confines positional encoding to local layers, and compares behavior on multiple-target retrieval, QA, and discrimination of semantically similar keys.
RkBg2Ytoer.key_idea: Confining positional encoding to local layers shifts in-context retrieval from positional to semantic mechanisms and selectively degrades positional-information representations.
RkBg2Ytoer.evidence: Mechanistic tracing across 22 open-weight models spanning eight families, a controlled pre-training ablation, and long-context behavioral tests.

EHgYupL4DU.one_liner: Text-guided diffusion for city layout generation using a condition-plan agent, global and local DiTs, and synchronized denoising.
EHgYupL4DU.problem: Large-scale urban semantic layouts from text must keep city-wide coherence and fine structure, but high-resolution generation is costly, sliding windows leave seams and sequential dependence, and text conditioning gives only coarse control over land use.
EHgYupL4DU.method: A compiler-grounded condition plan agent turns natural-language descriptions into executable zone-ratio conditions, a global DiT generates coarse city structure, and a local DiT refines fine-scale detail. Semantic consensus globally synchronized denoising (SC-GSD) denoises simultaneously for semantically consistent layouts.
EHgYupL4DU.key_idea: Simultaneous, semantically consensus-synchronized denoising (SC-GSD) across the layout, replacing sequential sliding-window sampling.
EHgYupL4DU.evidence: The abstract states extensive experiments on text-guided city generation but is cut off before any details.

y15RZMsTLJ.one_liner: TraceLock: lightweight learned controller deciding when a frozen diffusion language model commits tokens, reusable across decoding configurations.
y15RZMsTLJ.problem: Efficient diffusion-LM decoding requires deciding when to commit proposed tokens, which is usually calibrated separately for each decoding configuration.
y15RZMsTLJ.method: TraceLock labels an intermediate token proposal future-stable when it matches the final token of its completed trace and trains a shared contextual scorer on variable-length trace states. One checkpoint per backbone is deployed across tested window widths and generation lengths with a single global acceptance cutoff.
y15RZMsTLJ.key_idea: Train a shared scorer to predict whether an intermediate token proposal will match its final token in the completed diffusion trace, and commit tokens above one global cutoff.
y15RZMsTLJ.evidence: Experiments on mathematical reasoning, question answering, and code generation against heuristic and learned baselines, including Learn2PD under changing decoding windows.
y15RZMsTLJ.claimed_gains: Reports an improved quality-step tradeoff over heuristic and learned baselines and greater stability than Learn2PD when the decoding window changes, with no numbers stated.

ivjv3EHaaU.one_liner: Trajectory-conditioned flow matching generates control candidates that a learned dynamics predictor ranks under unknown and changing dynamics.
ivjv3EHaaU.problem: Learning-based controllers that assume fixed dynamics distributions adapt poorly when system dynamics are unknown or vary across environments.
ivjv3EHaaU.method: OMFM encodes streaming trajectories into shared context for a control generator and a dynamics predictor. The generator learns a Gibbs-weighted empirical trajectory distribution, and the predictor ranks generated control candidates by predicted objectives without additional environment interactions.
ivjv3EHaaU.key_idea: Condition flow-based control generation and learned candidate evaluation on shared context encoded from observed trajectories.
ivjv3EHaaU.evidence: OMFM is evaluated on five control tasks involving dynamical systems of varying complexity.

S6pFfmjr3X.one_liner: Data re-uploading and an all-to-all Ising entangler encode higher-order token interactions in single-qubit readouts.
S6pFfmjr3X.problem: A single budget-limited attention layer cannot compute certain higher-order token-matching tasks.
S6pFfmjr3X.method: DRIM uses a shallow quantum circuit with data re-uploading and an all-to-all non-Clifford entangler to form higher-order interactions. The analysis separately establishes attention matching limits, circuit monomial expressivity, and a barren-plateau-free guarantee for a local-design variant.
S6pFfmjr3X.key_idea: Repeatedly encode token data around non-Clifford entangling operations so higher-order interactions appear in single-qubit readouts.
S6pFfmjr3X.evidence: Theory addresses distinct matching and monomial targets, while validation-tuned experiments compare DRIM and attention models on hidden-subset parity over 8 seeds.
S6pFfmjr3X.claimed_gains: DRIM with 296 parameters solves every hidden-subset parity seed for k=3 to 6, versus 2 of 8 supports at k=5 and k=6 for single-layer attention and 6 of 8 at k=6 for a two-layer Transformer with 16× the parameters.

4IH19gY0yf.one_liner: Matched-waveform cross-dubs and controlled video transformations audit whether omni-modal models use visible speech articulation.
4IH19gY0yf.problem: Changes in speech recognition after adding video do not establish that models use visible articulation.
4IH19gY0yf.method: The audit tests silent word recognition, noisy speech, repeated or permuted frames, and cross-dubs with fixed auditory waveforms. Follow-up comparisons use native, reprocessed, and dubbed clips alongside a specialist audiovisual recognizer.
4IH19gY0yf.key_idea: Hold audio fixed while changing visual donors and video processing to test whether recognition follows visible speech content.
4IH19gY0yf.evidence: Experiments cover eight omni-modal models, comprising six open-weight and two closed-weight models, with specialist-recognizer comparisons and exploratory representation probes.
4IH19gY0yf.claimed_gains: A masker-only tail changes one model's audio-only accuracy by about eleven percentage points.

rJiqdyAaRm.one_liner: Transformer perturbation bounds and next-token margins certify unchanged chain-of-thought prefixes under bounded representation perturbations.
rJiqdyAaRm.problem: Existing empirical studies do not establish how long a reasoning prefix remains unchanged under bounded local perturbations.
rJiqdyAaRm.method: The paper formalizes trajectory stability as exact prefix preservation under bounded local representation perturbations. It combines finite-perturbation propagation bounds for causal Transformers with clean next-token decision margins to certify target prefixes.
rJiqdyAaRm.key_idea: Combine propagated representation-perturbation bounds with next-token decision margins to certify every token in a reasoning prefix.
rJiqdyAaRm.evidence: Theoretical sufficient conditions are evaluated on four reasoning models and three benchmarks for effects of perturbation location, magnitude, and prefix length.

WdGFmkkezN.one_liner: Deformable attention and learned cloth joints combine with Gaussian splatting for feed-forward animatable human reconstruction.
WdGFmkkezN.problem: Existing methods require per-subject optimization or produce static captures without adaptive clothing deformation.
WdGFmkkezN.method: FACt fuses 3D Gaussian representations with locally aligned image features through a deformable transformer. Adaptive cloth-joint learning extends Linear Blend Skinning beyond the SMPL-X kinematic template to animate clothing from sparse-view inputs.
WdGFmkkezN.key_idea: Fuse Gaussian representations with aligned image features and extend the skinning chain using learned cloth joints.
WdGFmkkezN.evidence: Experiments on real-world datasets evaluate reconstructed avatars under novel views and poses.

z9uTxlflad.one_liner: Recursive clustering of query-key feature pairs organizes Vision Transformer attention into interpretable semantic trees.
z9uTxlflad.problem: Vision Transformer attention weights remain noisy and difficult to interpret for localization, segmentation, and attribution.
z9uTxlflad.method: The paper concatenates query and key vectors into QK features and recursively clusters them into a QK tree for each attention head. Role cards visualize node behavior, supporting identification of position-indicator and object-centric nodes.
z9uTxlflad.key_idea: Recursively cluster concatenated query-key vectors into hierarchical nodes and visualize each node's functional role.
z9uTxlflad.evidence: Analyses show consistent semantic roles and localized spatial selectivity in tree nodes, while selecting an object-centric node supports object localization.

Fb65zGI9yN.one_liner: Sequence-level reverse-KL distillation combines one-step drifting with an offline critic to train continuous vision-language-action policies.
Fb65zGI9yN.problem: Chunk-level action training ignores long-horizon task success, while sequence-level reinforcement learning requires costly rollouts and closed-loop robot interaction.
Fb65zGI9yN.method: DriftOPD targets a reward-tilted demonstration distribution and decomposes sequence-level reverse KL into chunk-level and future-success terms. A one-step drifting objective optimizes the former, while a Q-function critic trained on offline demonstrations handles the latter.
Fb65zGI9yN.key_idea: Decompose sequence-level reverse KL into a chunk-level drifting objective and an offline-critic future term.
Fb65zGI9yN.evidence: Experiments span multiple VLA architectures in simulation and real-world manipulation, comparing one-step distillation baselines and multi-step teacher policies.

vlbufiEVvy.one_liner: Gated RGB-event fusion and support-generated residual updates adapt frozen video MLLMs to low-light reasoning.
vlbufiEVvy.problem: Low light destroys RGB appearance cues, while scarce paired event-language data limits use of complementary event-camera information.
vlbufiEVvy.method: LITE-Event combines modality-specific projectors with gated RGB-event fusion. A support-conditioned hypernetwork generates LoRA-style residual updates from a small non-target support set to adapt the interface while freezing encoders and the LLM.
vlbufiEVvy.key_idea: Fuse RGB and event features through a gated interface whose residual updates a hypernetwork generates from non-target support examples.
vlbufiEVvy.evidence: Training and evaluation use synthetic NExT-QA-Dark, curated EventLang-Dark, and real-world RealDark-Bench, with comparisons against enhancement-first and single-modality systems.
vlbufiEVvy.claimed_gains: LITE-Event reaches 85.0% on RealDark-Bench, exceeding the strongest enhancement-then-reason baseline by 5.2 points.

5GGLZvMduy.one_liner: Shared task specifications generate editing instructions and preservation predicates for evaluating agents' editable video project states.
5GGLZvMduy.problem: Rendered video quality alone does not verify whether an agent produces an editable project satisfying requested changes and preservation requirements.
5GGLZvMduy.method: TimelineBench derives atomic operations and reusable task templates from official editing tutorials, then varies media, targets, and parameters. Each operation links natural-language instructions to predicates checking requested changes and required preservation in project state.
5GGLZvMduy.key_idea: Generate instructions and project-state predicates from one structured specification so editing success checks both requested changes and preserved content.
5GGLZvMduy.evidence: The abstract reports 1,453 tasks from 48 operations and 121 templates, evaluating seven agents in OpenCut-TL and matched tasks in Adobe Premiere Pro.
5GGLZvMduy.claimed_gains: GPT-6 Sol achieves 89.40% overall and 62.58% animation-task success in OpenCut-TL, while its success on 56 matched tasks drops from 83.93% in OpenCut-TL to 62.50% in Premiere Pro.

tbkbyR3ExP.one_liner: Converting frozen image-to-video rewards into image preferences trains text-to-image generators to produce better video anchors.
tbkbyR3ExP.problem: Anchor-image aesthetic and quality scores poorly predict downstream video quality, and image-reward tuning can reduce video rewards.
tbkbyR3ExP.method: Golden Anchor Learning evaluates candidate anchor images through videos generated by a frozen image-to-video model. It converts downstream video rewards into image-level preferences for offline DPO of the text-to-image generator.
tbkbyR3ExP.key_idea: Rank candidate anchor images by the videos they induce in a frozen generator, then train the image generator with those preferences.
tbkbyR3ExP.evidence: The analysis tests correlations between anchor metrics and downstream video quality, while the TL;DR reports quality and motion gains that transfer to unseen image-to-video models.

8iPy2VA94x.one_liner: Evolving semantic graphs, stabilizing dual experts, and exploring uncertain feature boundaries support semi-supervised few-shot class-incremental learning.
8iPy2VA94x.problem: Static pseudo-labeling and incremental adaptation struggle with unreliable semantic discovery, representation drift, and poorly characterized boundaries under sparse supervision.
8iPy2VA94x.method: DSE-SSF propagates information over an evolving semantic manifold and uses temporal consistency with adaptive uncertainty calibration to stabilize dual experts. Boundary-aware feature exploration examines uncertain regions to refine decision boundaries.
8iPy2VA94x.key_idea: Couple evolving semantic-graph propagation with uncertainty-calibrated dual experts and exploration of uncertain feature regions in a closed learning loop.

BXdo3p6gig.one_liner: Penalizing a flow-matching velocity field's action-history Jacobian limits amplification of past-action errors in imitation policies.
BXdo3p6gig.problem: Policies conditioned on correlated expert action histories can amplify their own execution errors when generated actions re-enter policy inputs.
BXdo3p6gig.method: PRIM regularizes the velocity field's Jacobian with respect to action history in flow-matching behavior cloning. The analysis relates conditional predictability to history sensitivity and derives recursive error propagation through both dynamics and history inputs.
BXdo3p6gig.key_idea: Penalize the flow velocity field's Jacobian with respect to past actions to control propagation of errors through recurrent history conditioning.
BXdo3p6gig.evidence: Theory gives sufficient conditions for bounded accumulated error, and LIBERO-90 experiments compare direct history conditioning with Jacobian regularization.

8UJQWVJK2w.one_liner: Coupling biomedical discovery memory with staged program execution guides Monte Carlo graph search for biomedical machine-learning tasks.
8UJQWVJK2w.problem: Agentic biomedical systems struggle to coordinate evidence acquisition, program construction, outcome reuse, and validation within a search budget.
8UJQWVJK2w.method: BioDyad combines scientific and engineering hierarchies inside Monte Carlo graph search. The scientific hierarchy links prior guidance and iterative discovery to plan–outcome memory, while engineering stages progress from smoke execution to validation and full-data retraining.
8UJQWVJK2w.key_idea: Use plan–outcome memory to connect iterative biomedical discovery with candidate program search, allocating execution through progressively stronger evaluation stages.
8UJQWVJK2w.evidence: On 76 BioXArena tasks with two hours per task and three matched LLM backends, BioDyad ranks highest in penalized score and success among the evaluated agents and one-shot baseline.

ptbDkGB08q.one_liner: Testing interactions between biological component subspaces against established rules assesses genomic foundation models' scientific reliability.
ptbDkGB08q.problem: Similar downstream predictive scores can hide differences in biological mechanisms and scientific reliability within genomic foundation models.
